readingText.title: 겠의 세 가지 얼굴
readingText.body: 겠은 단순히 미래를 말하는 표현이 아니에요. 직원이 손님에게 주문을 확인하겠습니다라고 말하면, 그냥 미래 계획이 아니라 지금 책임지고 처리하겠다는 약속처럼 들려요. 반대로 자료를 보니 결과가 달라지겠네요는 자료라는 근거를 보고 내린 추론이에요. 또 죄송하지만 참석하기 어렵겠습니다처럼 말하면 못 가요보다 훨씬 정중하고 부드러운 거절이 돼요. 그래서 겠을 볼 때는 먼저 상황을 봐야 해요. 내가 하겠다는 약속인지, 근거를 보고 추측하는지, 아니면 말을 부드럽게 만드는지 구분해야 자연스럽게 쓸 수 있어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: 겠 is not simply a future marker. When a staff member says 'I will check the order,' it sounds like a responsible promise, not just a future plan. By contrast, 'Looking at the data, the result will change' is an inference from evidence. And saying 'I'm sorry, but it will be difficult for me to attend' is a much more courteous and softened refusal than simply saying 'I can't go.' So when you see 겠, look at the situation first. Is it a promise that I will do something, an inference from evidence, or a way to soften speech?

comprehensionQuestions.question: 직원이 확인하겠습니다라고 말하면 어떤 느낌이에요?
자료를 보니 결과가 달라지겠네요는 어떤 겠이에요?
참석하기 어렵겠습니다는 왜 써요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 거절을 정중하고 부드럽게 말하기 위해 써요.

culturalNote.title: 서비스 말투의 책임감
culturalNote.body: In Korean service and workplace settings, -겠습니다 often signals professionalism. 제가 확인하겠습니다, 바로 처리하겠습니다, 도와드리겠습니다 all tell the listener that the speaker is taking responsibility. In private plans, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 is more natural. In refusals, 어렵겠습니다 softens the message without sounding evasive.
culturalNote.tip: If the sentence is about a promise to the listener, try -겠습니다. If it is a private plan, use -(으)ㄹ 거예요. If it is a cautious guess, use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is a formal service commitment?
options: 주문은 제가 바로 확인할 것 같아요.
inlineExercises.explanation: -겠습니다 marks a formal commitment controlled by the speaker.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 겠 for inference from evidence?
inlineExercises.explanation: The data gives evidence for the speaker's inference.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is the most courteous formal refusal?
inlineExercises.explanation: 어렵겠습니다 softens the refusal in formal speech.

inlineExercises.prompt: 자료___ 많겠네요. (The materials must be a lot.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 많다 describes the amount of 자료, so 자료 takes 가. 겠네요 gives an inference from what you see or hear.

inlineExercises.prompt: 제가 바로 ___ . (확인하다 → formal commitment)
inlineExercises.explanation: -겠습니다 is a formal commitment in service or professional speech. 확인하다 becomes 확인하겠습니다.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'I will help you right away.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 도와드리겠습니다 is formal and respectful. 바로 adds the service promise “right away.”

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'That must be hard.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -겠네요 gives an inference or empathetic reaction from evidence. 힘드시겠네요 is polite and considerate.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the mixed formal future: '확인할 거겠습니다.'
inlineExercises.explanation: Do not stack -ㄹ 거예요 and -겠습니다. In formal service speech, use 확인하겠습니다.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 겠 for inference, not a promise?
inlineExercises.explanation: 많겠네요 is an inference from evidence. 처리하겠습니다 and 참석하겠습니다 are formal commitments.

inlineExercises.prompt: Write a courteous formal refusal: 'I think attending will be difficult.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 어렵겠습니다 softens a formal refusal. 참석하기 turns attending into the thing that is difficult.

bullets: Commitment: 제가 확인하겠습니다, 제가 처리하겠습니다.
Inference: 자료를 보니 결과가 달라지겠네요, 많이 피곤하시겠네요.
Softened refusal: 참석하기 어렵겠습니다.
-(으)ㄹ 거예요 is an ordinary future plan; -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 is a tentative guess.

writingTask.prompt: A customer emailed asking about their order. Reply: say you'll check it right away, then add a careful guess about when the result will come.
writingTask.hint: Use V-겠습니다/겠어요 for your own intention (확인하겠습니다), and A/V-겠네요 or -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 for a soft guess.
writingTask.model: 주문은 제가 바로 확인하겠습니다. 자료를 처리하고 결과를 알려 드리겠습니다. 오늘 안에 끝날 것 같아요.
writingTask.modelEn: I'll check your order right away. I'll process the materials and let you know the result. I think it'll be done within today.

canDo: State my own intention politely with V-겠습니다 / V-겠어요 (확인하겠습니다)
Make a careful inference from evidence with A/V-겠네요 (바쁘겠네요)
Talk about a future plan with V-(으)ㄹ 거예요 (기다릴 거예요)
Soften a statement into a tentative guess with -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 (끝날 것 같아요)

chapters.title: Unreal Conditionals
chapters.goal: Talk about a past choice that could have gone differently.
chapters.scenario: You missed a bus, found out too late, or wish you had said something earlier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I heard you were late for the interview yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 늦지 않았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. beoseureul nochiji anatdeoramyeon neutji anasseul tende-yo.
dialogue.en: Yes. If I had not missed the bus, I would not have been late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If you had known in advance, would you have taken a taxi?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 조금만 일찍 나왔으면 좋았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. jogeumman iljjik nawasseumyeon joasseul tende-yo.
dialogue.en: Yes. It would have been nice if I had left just a little earlier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 다음엔 전날에 길을 확인해 두면 좋겠어요.
dialogue.romanization: daeumen jeonnare gireul hwaginhae dumyeon jokesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Next time, it would be good to check the route the day before.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one regret about information you did not know, one missed-transport situation, and one relationship regret using -았/었으면 or -았/었더라면.
chapters.realLifeTask: Turn one real regret into an unreal conditional sentence.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a missed condition. Answer with the missed condition first, then a hypothetical result: -았/었더라면 ... -았/었을 거예요.
chapters.review: Can you make both halves hypothetical, instead of mixing a past condition with a plain real result?

beginnerGuide.title: Start from the missed condition
beginnerGuide.body: These sentences begin from something that did not happen: 미리 알다, 일찍 도착하다, 버스를 놓치지 않다, 바로 사과하다.

beginnerGuide.title: Make the result unreal too
beginnerGuide.body: After -았/었으면 or -았/었더라면, the second half usually needs -았/었을 텐데, -았/었을 거예요, or -았/었을지도 몰라요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -더라면 for stronger hindsight
beginnerGuide.body: -았/었더라면 sounds more reflective and certain that the condition was missed. It fits regret, advice after the fact, and imagining a different outcome.

checkpoints: I can use -았/었으면 for a soft regret or wish.
I can use -았/었더라면 for an unreal past condition.
I can pair the condition with -았/었을 텐데요 or -았/었을 거예요.

curriculumTrack.label: B2 Advanced Control
curriculumTrack.description: Causatives, counterfactuals, nominalisation, attitude endings, discourse control, and register switching.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Talk about a past choice that could have gone differently.
exitTask.prompt: Turn one real regret into an unreal conditional sentence.

sampleAnswer.ko: 미리 알았더라면 더 일찍 출발했을 거예요.
sampleAnswer.en: If I had known in advance, I would have left earlier.

checklist: I can use -았/었으면 for a soft regret or wish.
I can use -았/었더라면 for an unreal past condition.
I can pair the condition with -았/었을 텐데요 or -았/었을 거예요.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: You are looking back at a missed notice, a late arrival, and a conversation you should have handled differently. This chapter teaches the Korean frame for saying, "If that had happened differently, the result would have changed."
objectives: Build counterfactual sentences from a missed past condition.
Keep the result clause hypothetical with -았/었을 텐데, -았/었을 거예요, or -았/었을지도 몰라요.
Use regret vocabulary such as 미리, 놓치다, 후회하다, 결과, 달라지다, and 사과하다 in the same scenes as the grammar.
hook.whyItMatters: Without this frame, learners often say a plain past sentence and only add "if" in English. Korean needs the condition and the result to both show that you are imagining a different past.

grammarNotes.title: V-았/었으면 좋겠어요 — a wish ("I wish / I hope")
grammarNotes.func: Expresses a wish that the present situation were different, or a hope for something to come true. The past-shaped -았/었- here is NOT real past tense; it sets the wish against current reality. English renders it as "I wish..." (reality is the opposite) or "I hope..." (still possible).

formTable.ex: 오다 → 봄이 왔으면 좋겠어요 (I wish spring would come)

formTable.when: Stem ends in any other vowel
formTable.ex: 있다 → 시간이 있었으면 좋겠어요 (I wish I had time)
건강하다 → 건강했으면 좋겠어요 (I hope you stay healthy)
비가 그쳤으면 좋겠다 (I wish the rain would stop)

examples.en: I hope the weather is nice this weekend.
examples.note: A future hope that is still possible; -았- does not mean past here.

examples.en: I hope the exam isn't too hard.
examples.note: Negative wish: 어렵지 않다 takes -았으면 just like any other stem.

examples.en: I wish a friend were here beside me right now.
examples.note: 지금 makes it clearly contrary to present fact — a true 'I wish' reading.

examples.en: I hope I get up early tomorrow.
examples.note: The speaker's own hope/resolve; the wish points forward in time.

keyPoint.label: -았/었으면 좋겠어요 vs -(으)면 좋겠어요
keyPoint.body: Both mean 'I wish/hope.' The -았/었- version is by far the more common, natural choice in everyday speech and leans toward wishing reality were currently otherwise. The plain -(으)면 좋겠어요 sounds a bit more like a neutral 'it would be good if...'. When in doubt, use -았/었으면 좋겠어요.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 좋겠어요 is pronounced [조케써요]: the ㅎ of 좋 and the ㄱ of 겠 fuse into aspirated [ㅋ], and 겠어요 links smoothly as [게써요].

drill.instruction: Turn each plain wish into a full -았/었으면 좋겠어요 sentence.
items: 방이 조금 더 따뜻하다 → 방이 조금 더 _______ 좋겠어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'I wish' tempts learners to reach for 원하다 ('want'). Korean does not use 원하다 for wishing a situation were different. The fixed frame is -았/었으면 좋겠어요, literally 'it would be good if it had been (so).' Don't translate 'wish' as 원하다.

grammarNotes.title: V-았/었으면 … -았/었을 텐데요 — a past counterfactual with regret
grammarNotes.func: States a counterfactual about the past: a condition that did NOT happen, and the result that therefore did NOT happen. -았/었으면 marks the unreal past condition; the result clause stays hypothetical with -았/었을 텐데요 ('would have...'). The 텐데 ending softens it into a wistful 'but it wasn't so.'

formTable.ex: 가다 → 갔을 텐데요 (I would have gone)
공부했으면 합격했을 텐데요 (if I'd studied, I'd have passed)
일찍 출발했으면 안 늦었을 텐데요 (if I'd left early, I wouldn't have been late)

examples.ko: 미리 공지를 알았으면 시험 준비를 더 했을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: miri gongjireul arasseumyeon siheom junbireul deo haesseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I had known about the notice in advance, I would have prepared more for the exam.
examples.note: 미리 알다 from the chapter's regret vocabulary; the result also stays unreal with 했을 텐데요.

examples.ko: 조금만 더 일찍 일어났으면 버스를 탔을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: jogeumman deo iljjik ireonasseumyeon beoseureul tasseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I had gotten up just a little earlier, I would have caught the bus.
examples.note: A typical regret scene: a small unmet condition with a clear missed result.

examples.ko: 우산을 가져갔으면 비를 안 맞았을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: usaneul gajyeogasseumyeon bireul an majasseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I had taken an umbrella, I wouldn't have gotten rained on.
examples.note: 가져갔으면 strongly implies the speaker did NOT take one.

examples.ko: 그때 바로 사과했으면 사이가 안 나빠졌을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: geuttae baro sagwahaesseumyeon saiga an nappajyeosseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I had apologized right then, the relationship wouldn't have gone bad.
examples.note: 사과하다 fits the regret vocabulary of the chapter; 달라지다/나빠지다 carry the changed outcome.

keyPoint.label: Keep the result clause hypothetical
keyPoint.body: Whichever condition you use, the result must also be marked unreal: -았/었을 텐데요, -았/었을 거예요, or -았/었을지도 몰라요 ('might have'). Never finish a past counterfactual with a plain past or present verb — that cancels the 'would have' meaning. 텐데요 adds the softest, most wistful tone of the three.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 텐데요 is [텐데요], no special change. Note 갔을 텐데요 → [가쓸 텐데요]: 갔 closes as [갇] and links into 을 as [가쓸].

drill.instruction: Complete each counterfactual so both the condition and the result stay past-hypothetical.
drill.model: 약을 먹다 / 안 아프다 → 약을 먹었으면 안 아팠을 텐데요.
items: 전화하다 / 만나다 → 전화______ 우리가 만났을 텐데요.
표를 예매하다 / 자리가 있다 → 표를 예매______ 자리가 있었을 텐데요.
조심하다 / 안 다치다 → 조심______ 안 ______ 텐데요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners set up the 'if had' clause correctly but then drop into a plain present/future result ('I call' / 'I will call'). In Korean the result of a past counterfactual must itself be marked unreal: -았/었을 텐데요. A plain result clause cancels the 'would have' meaning.

grammarNotes.title: V-았/었더라면 … -았/었을 거예요 — a stronger, more reflective counterfactual
grammarNotes.func: Replays a missed past from a reflective distance: 'if (only) it had happened, the result would have...'. -았/었더라면 marks the unreal past condition with a heavier, more regretful tone than -았/었으면; the result stays hypothetical with -았/었을 거예요 ('would have').

formTable.ex: 보다 → 봤을 거예요 (I would have seen it)
조금만 일찍 도착했더라면 시험을 봤을 거예요 (if I'd arrived a bit earlier, I'd have taken the exam)

examples.ko: 조금만 일찍 도착했더라면 시험을 볼 수 있었을 거예요.
examples.romanization: jogeumman iljjik dochakaetdeoramyeon siheomeul bol su isseosseul geoyeyo.
examples.en: If I had arrived just a little earlier, I could have taken the exam.
examples.note: Arriving early didn't happen, so the result stays hypothetical too.

examples.ko: 지도를 미리 봤더라면 길을 안 잃었을 거예요.
examples.romanization: jidoreul miri bwatdeoramyeon gireul an ireosseul geoyeyo.
examples.en: If I had looked at the map in advance, I wouldn't have gotten lost.
examples.note: 봤더라면 = the look-up that never happened; 안 잃었을 거예요 = the avoided result.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 들었더라면 바로 전화했을 거예요.
examples.romanization: geu sosigeul deureotdeoramyeon baro jeonhwahaesseul geoyeyo.
examples.en: If I had heard the news, I would have called right away.
examples.note: Both clauses carry past 았/었; the whole sentence is firmly counterfactual.

examples.en: If I had apologized then, the outcome would have been different.
examples.note: 사과하다, 결과, 달라지다 are all the chapter's target regret words.

keyPoint.label: -았/었더라면 vs -았/었으면
keyPoint.body: Both open a past counterfactual, but -았/었더라면 is heavier and more clearly regretful — it almost always implies 'and that's a shame, because it didn't happen.' -았/었으면 is more neutral and far more common in casual speech. In friendly chat 더라면 can sound dramatic, so friends often just use -았/었으면. The result clause stays hypothetical either way.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 봤더라면 → [봗떠라면]: the ㅆ of 봤 closes to [ㄷ] before a consonant, and ㄷ of 더 tenses to [떠]. 들었더라면 → [드럳떠라면] follows the same tensing.

drill.instruction: Complete each -았/었더라면 … -았/었을 거예요 counterfactual.
drill.model: 약을 먹다 / 안 아프다 → 약을 먹었더라면 안 아팠을 거예요.
items: 전화하다 / 만나다 → 전화______ 우리가 만났을 거예요.
표를 예매하다 / 자리가 있다 → 표를 예매______ 자리가 있었을 거예요.
조심하다 / 안 다치다 → 조심______ 안 ______ 거예요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners sometimes try to stack -으면 and -더라면 together. They are two different conditional endings and cannot combine. Use one or the other directly on the past stem: 알았으면 OR 알았더라면, never 알았으면더라면.

grammarNotes.title: V-지 않았더라면 — a negative counterfactual ("if … hadn't …")
grammarNotes.func: Forms the negative side of a past counterfactual: 'if (something) had NOT happened.' Because the event DID happen, a certain (often bad) result followed — and you imagine the opposite past. It pairs with a hypothetical result clause.

formTable.ex: 놓치다 → 놓치지 않았더라면 (if I hadn't missed it)
못 봤더라면 (if I hadn't been able to see it)
포기하지 않았더라면 합격했을지도 몰라요 (if I hadn't given up, I might have passed)

examples.ko: 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 면접에 늦지 않았을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: beoseureul nochiji anatdeoramyeon myeonjeobe neutji anasseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I hadn't missed the bus, I wouldn't have been late for the interview.
examples.note: 놓치다 (to miss) is the chapter's regret vocabulary; 놓치지 않았더라면 keeps the negative inside the condition.

examples.en: If I hadn't given up, I might have passed.
examples.note: -았/었을지도 몰라요 keeps the outcome uncertain but still unreal.

examples.ko: 그때 화를 내지 않았더라면 지금 후회하지 않았을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: geuttae hwareul naeji anatdeoramyeon jigeum huhoehaji anasseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I hadn't gotten angry then, I wouldn't be regretting it now.
examples.note: 후회하다 is a target word; the result uses 텐데요 for present regret.

examples.ko: 네가 도와주지 않았더라면 저는 실패했을 거예요.
examples.romanization: nega dowajuji anatdeoramyeon jeoneun silpaehaesseul geoyeyo.
examples.en: If you hadn't helped me, I would have failed.
examples.note: A common gratitude use: the negative counterfactual highlights how crucial the real help was.

keyPoint.label: -지 않았더라면 vs -았/었더라면
keyPoint.body: Use affirmative -았/었더라면 to imagine an action you wish HAD happened ('if I had studied'). Use -지 않았더라면 to imagine an action you wish had NOT happened ('if I hadn't missed it'). The result clause works identically for both; only the polarity of the condition changes.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 않았더라면 → [아낟떠라면]: the ㅎ of 않 is silent so 않았 reads [아낟] (the ㅆ closing to [ㄷ] before 더), and 더 tenses to [떠].

drill.instruction: Rewrite each affirmative idea as a negative counterfactual ('if … hadn't …').

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 안 비가 왔더라면 소풍을 갔을 거예요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 비가 오지 않았더라면 소풍을 갔을 거예요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners often put 안 before the noun (안 비가). With this frame, the clean choice is long negation V-지 않았더라면. If you do use short 안, it goes directly before the verb (비가 안 왔더라면), never before the subject noun.

grammarNotes.title: -(으)면 vs -았/었으면 — open condition vs missed condition
grammarNotes.func: Distinguishes a real, still-open condition from an unreal, already-missed one. Plain V-(으)면 leaves the door open ('if/when you have time'). Past-shaped V-았/었으면 usually looks backward at a condition that did NOT happen, setting up a counterfactual result.

formTable.ex: 시간이 있으면 같이 확인해요 (if you have time, let's check together)
시간이 있었으면 같이 확인했을 텐데요 (if there had been time, we'd have checked)
준비하면 덜 불안해요 / 준비했으면 안 늦었을 텐데요
미리 준비하면 덜 불안해요 (if you prepare ahead, you feel less anxious)

examples.en: If you have time, let's check it together.
examples.note: An open condition — time may still be available, so the result is a real plan.

examples.en: If there had been time, we would have checked it together.
examples.note: The past form turns the same idea into hindsight about a missed chance.

examples.en: If you prepare in advance, you feel less anxious.
examples.note: A reusable rule, so plain V-(으)면 is correct — not counterfactual.

examples.ko: 그때 미리 알았으면 놓치지 않았을 거예요.
examples.romanization: geuttae miri arasseumyeon nochiji anasseul geoyeyo.
examples.en: If I had known in advance then, I wouldn't have missed it.
examples.note: 그때 plus the unreal result shows this is a missed past, not an open rule.

keyPoint.label: Let context and the result decide the reading
keyPoint.body: The past form alone doesn't always mean counterfactual — context and the result clause decide. A simple test: can the condition still happen? If yes, plain V-(으)면 with a real result is usually enough. If it's already too late, use V-았/었으면 and keep the result unreal (-았/었을 텐데요 / -았/었을 거예요).

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 있었으면 → [이써쓰면]: 있 closes as [읻] then links into 었 as [이써], and 었으면 connects as [쓰면]. 있으면 (open) stays lighter as [이쓰면].

drill.instruction: Choose -(으)면 for an open condition or -았/었으면 for a missed one, then complete the sentence.
drill.model: 시간이 있다 (open) → 시간이 있으면 같이 확인해요.
items: 내일 비가 안 오다 (open hope) → 내일 비가 안 ____ 좋겠어요.
그때 일찍 출발하다 (missed) → 그때 일찍 ______ 안 늦었을 텐데요.
주말에 날씨가 좋다 (still possible) → 주말에 날씨가 ____ 소풍을 가요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 어제 시간이 있으면 같이 봤을 거예요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 어제 시간이 있었으면 같이 봤을 거예요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: For a clearly past, missed condition (어제 'yesterday'), the plain present -(으)면 clashes with the past result 봤을 거예요. Match the condition to the timeframe: a missed past needs -았/었으면, not plain -(으)면.

exampleSentence.ko: 미리 알았으면 준비를 더 했을 텐데요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had known in advance, I would have prepared more.
exampleSentence.note: 알았으면 is one of the most common starting points for regret.

exampleSentence.ko: 미리 말했더라면 문제가 커지지 않았을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had said it in advance, the problem would not have gotten bigger.
exampleSentence.note: 미리 naturally pairs with 알다, 말하다, 준비하다, and 예약하다.

exampleSentence.ko: 서류를 미리 준비했더라면 접수를 놓치지 않았을 텐데요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had prepared the documents in advance, I would not have missed the application.
exampleSentence.note: 준비했더라면 turns a practical mistake into a counterfactual condition.

exampleSentence.ko: 조금만 일찍 도착했더라면 시험을 볼 수 있었을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had arrived just a little earlier, I could have taken the exam.
exampleSentence.note: 시험을 보다 is the fixed phrase for taking an exam.

exampleSentence.ko: 조금만 일찍 나왔으면 버스를 놓치지 않았을 텐데요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had left just a little earlier, I would not have missed the bus.
exampleSentence.note: 조금만 일찍 is a very natural regret chunk.

exampleSentence.ko: 제시간에 도착했더라면 면접을 볼 수 있었을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had arrived on time, I could have had the interview.
exampleSentence.note: 도착했더라면 is useful for exams, interviews, trains, and appointments.

exampleSentence.ko: 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 늦지 않았을 텐데요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had not missed the bus, I would not have been late.
exampleSentence.note: Use 놓치다 for transport, chances, deadlines, and timing.

exampleSentence.ko: 그 버스를 탔더라면 약속 시간에 맞췄을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had taken that bus, I would have made it on time for the appointment.
exampleSentence.note: Transport words make counterfactuals concrete: take it, miss it, arrive late.

exampleSentence.ko: 바로 사과했더라면 이렇게 후회하지 않았을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had apologized right away, I would not regret it like this.
exampleSentence.note: 후회하다 often appears in the result clause.

exampleSentence.ko: 그때 말하지 않은 게 아직도 후회예요.
exampleSentence.en: Not saying it back then is still a regret.
exampleSentence.note: Noun form 후회 works when the regret itself is the topic.

exampleSentence.ko: 마지막까지 포기하지 않았더라면 결과가 달라졌을지도 몰라요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had not given up until the end, the result might have changed.
exampleSentence.note: 결과가 달라지다 is the key outcome phrase.

exampleSentence.ko: 그때 선택을 바꿨더라면 지금 상황이 달라졌을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had changed my choice then, the situation would be different now.
exampleSentence.note: 달라졌을 거예요 is a natural result clause for counterfactuals.

exampleSentence.ko: 그 기회를 잡았더라면 다른 회사에 갔을지도 몰라요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had taken that opportunity, I might have gone to a different company.
exampleSentence.note: 기회를 잡다 and 기회를 놓치다 are both useful in hindsight.

exampleSentence.ko: 그때 솔직하게 말했더라면 오해가 풀렸을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had spoken honestly then, the misunderstanding would have cleared up.
exampleSentence.note: 말하다 becomes powerful in regret scenes because one sentence could have changed the relationship.

exampleSentence.ko: 먼저 사과했더라면 아직 어색하지 않았을 텐데요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had apologized first, it would not still be awkward.
exampleSentence.note: 사과했더라면 fits relationship repair after the fact.

exampleSentence.ko: 그때 멈췄더라면 일이 이렇게 커지지 않았을 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: If I had stopped back then, this would not have gotten this big.
exampleSentence.note: 그때 anchors the regret in a specific past moment.

exampleSentence.en: If I had not given up, I might have passed.
exampleSentence.note: 포기하지 않았더라면 is a high-frequency negative counterfactual.

exampleSentence.en: If I had solved the last question, I would have passed.
exampleSentence.note: 합격하다 belongs naturally in exam-regret counterfactuals.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two friends compare three regrets after a hard week: a missed notice, a missed bus, and a message that should have been sent sooner.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 어제 공지를 미리 알았으면 시험 준비를 더 했을 텐데.
lines.romanization: eoje gongjireul miri arasseumyeon siheom junbireul deo haesseul tende.
lines.en: If I had known about the notice in advance yesterday, I would have prepared more for the exam.
lines.grammarNote: 알았으면 sets up a missed information condition; 했을 텐데 gives the unreal result.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그래도 포기하지 않았더라면 마지막 문제는 풀 수 있었을지도 몰라.
lines.romanization: geuraedo pogihaji anatdeoramyeon majimak munjeneun pul su isseosseuljido molla.
lines.en: Still, if you had not given up, you might have been able to solve the last question.
lines.grammarNote: The negative form is 포기하지 않았더라면, with the negation before -더라면.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 맞아. 결과가 조금은 달라졌을 것 같아.
lines.romanization: maja. gyeolgwaga jogeumeun dallajyeosseul geot gata.
lines.en: You're right. The result might have been a little different.
lines.grammarNote: 달라졌을 것 같아 keeps the result hypothetical.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 나는 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 면접에 늦지 않았을 텐데.
lines.romanization: naneun beoseureul notchiji anatdeoramyeon myeonjeobe neutji anatseul tende.
lines.en: If I had not missed the bus, I would not have been late for the interview.
lines.grammarNote: A practical transport regret: 놓치지 않았더라면 + 늦지 않았을 텐데.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그때 다른 길로 갔으면 도착 시간이 달라졌을지도 몰라.
lines.romanization: geuttae dareun gillo gasseumyeon dochak sigani dallajyeosseuljido molla.
lines.en: If you had taken a different route then, the arrival time might have changed.
lines.grammarNote: -았/었으면 is lighter than -더라면 and works in casual reflection.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그리고 친구한테 바로 사과했더라면 아직 이렇게 어색하지는 않았을 거야.
lines.romanization: geurigo chinguhante baro sagwahaetdeoramyeon ajik ireoke eosaekajineun anatseul geoya.
lines.en: And if I had apologized to my friend right away, it probably would not still be this awkward.
lines.grammarNote: 사과했더라면 shows relationship hindsight, not only test or travel regret.

readingText.title: 그때 알았더라면
readingText.body: 민서는 시험 전날 공지가 바뀐 것을 늦게 알았다. 미리 알았으면 자료를 다시 확인했을 텐데, 그대로 시험장에 갔다. 지훈은 면접 날 버스를 놓쳤다. 조금만 일찍 나왔더라면 제시간에 도착했을 거라고 생각했다. 두 사람은 나중에 서로의 이야기를 듣고 같은 말을 했다. "그때 바로 알았더라면 결과가 달라졌을지도 몰라." 하지만 마지막에는 후회만 반복하지 않기로 했다. 다음에는 중요한 공지를 미리 확인하고, 늦을 것 같으면 바로 연락하고, 마음에 걸리는 말은 빨리 사과하기로 했다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo found out late that the notice had changed before the exam. If she had known in advance, she would have checked the materials again, but she went to the exam room as she was. Jihoon missed the bus on interview day. He thought that if he had left a little earlier, he would have arrived on time. Later, after hearing each other's stories, they said the same thing: "If we had known right away back then, the result might have changed." In the end, they decided not to repeat only regret. Next time they would check important notices in advance, contact people right away if they might be late, and apologize quickly for words that bothered them.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 무엇을 늦게 알았어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 시험 전날 공지가 바뀐 것을 늦게 알았어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 지훈은 왜 면접에 늦을 뻔했어요?
두 사람은 다음에 무엇을 하기로 했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 중요한 공지를 미리 확인하고, 늦을 것 같으면 바로 연락하고, 마음에 걸리는 말은 빨리 사과하기로 했어요.

culturalNote.title: 후회 말하기는 자책보다 부드럽게
culturalNote.body: In Korean, counterfactual regret is often softened with -을 텐데요, 아쉽다, or 그랬으면 좋았을 텐데요. This lets you acknowledge the mistake without sounding as if you are attacking yourself or blaming the listener. In a workplace or classroom, 미리 말씀드렸으면 좋았을 텐데요 is safer than a blunt 제가 잘못했어요 when you are reflecting, not formally apologizing.
culturalNote.tip: Use -더라면 when you want a clear hindsight frame. Use -았/었으면 좋겠어요 when you are expressing a wish more than analyzing a result.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses regret about not knowing earlier?
inlineExercises.explanation: The condition is missed in the past, and the result is also hypothetical with -했을 텐데요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Choose the correct negative counterfactual.
inlineExercises.explanation: The negative must be inside the past condition: -지 않았더라면.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which result clause stays hypothetical?
inlineExercises.explanation: -았/었을지도 몰라요 marks an imagined different result.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete the regret: 바로 사과했더라면 이렇게 ____ 않았을 텐데요. (use 후회하다)
inlineExercises.explanation: 후회하지 않았을 텐데요 means "I would not regret it."

inlineExercises.prompt: 버스___ 놓쳤더라면 늦었을 거예요. (If I had missed the bus...)
inlineExercises.explanation: 놓치다 takes the thing missed as an object, so 버스를 fits. The counterfactual ending shows this did not actually happen.

inlineExercises.prompt: 미리 ___ 준비했을 거예요. (알다 → stronger past counterfactual)
inlineExercises.explanation: -았/었더라면 makes a reflective past counterfactual. 알다 becomes 알았더라면.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'If I had known in advance, I would have prepared.'
inlineExercises.explanation: The condition is a missed past condition, so 알았더라면 fits. The result stays hypothetical with 했을 거예요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete: 바로 사과했더라면 이렇게 ____ 않았을 텐데요. (use 되다)
inlineExercises.explanation: 되지 않았을 텐데요 keeps the result hypothetical and regretful. It means the situation would not have become like this.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the regret: '미리 알면 준비했을 텐데요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: For a missed past condition, use 알았으면, not the open condition 알면. The result clause 했을 텐데요 stays hypothetical.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which condition is clearly about a missed past chance?
inlineExercises.explanation: -았/었더라면 points to a past condition that did not happen. The other choices are open condition or real past result.

bullets: Use V-았/었으면 for a lighter missed condition and V-았/었더라면 for stronger hindsight.
After a counterfactual condition, keep the result unreal: -았/었을 텐데요, -았/었을 거예요, or -았/었을지도 몰라요.
For negative conditions, place the negation before -더라면: 포기하지 않았더라면, 놓치지 않았더라면.
The most useful vocabulary set is not random: 미리 알다, 일찍 도착하다, 버스를 놓치다, 결과가 달라지다, 후회하다, 사과하다.

writingTask.prompt: You missed the bus and were late for an exam. Write a short note regretting it: one wish, and one 'if I had... I would have...' counterfactual.
writingTask.hint: Use V-았/었으면 좋겠어요 for a wish, and V-았/었으면 … -았/었을 텐데요 (or -았/었더라면 … -았/었을 거예요) for the missed past.
writingTask.model: 조금 더 일찍 일어났으면 좋겠어요. 미리 준비했더라면 버스를 놓치지 않았을 거예요. 일찍 도착했으면 시험을 잘 봤을 텐데요.
writingTask.modelEn: I wish I'd gotten up a little earlier. If I had prepared in advance, I wouldn't have missed the bus. If I'd arrived early, I would have done well on the exam.

canDo: Express a wish that things were different with V-았/었으면 좋겠어요 (일찍 일어났으면 좋겠어요)
Regret a missed past with V-았/었으면 … -았/었을 텐데요 (도착했으면 … 봤을 텐데요)
State a reflective counterfactual with V-았/었더라면 … -았/었을 거예요 (준비했더라면 … 놓치지 않았을 거예요)
Tell an open condition (-(으)면) from a missed one (-았/었으면)

chapters.title: Nominalisation — 기 vs 는 것
chapters.goal: Turn actions into nouns without making the sentence heavy.
chapters.scenario: You talk about studying, habits, goals, and things you saw someone do.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 매일 운동하기는 어렵지만 건강을 위해 필요해요.
dialogue.romanization: maeil undonghagineun eoryeopjiman geongangeul wihae piryohaeyo.
dialogue.en: Exercising every day is hard, but it is necessary for health.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I decided to start with walking first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 친구가 매일 걷는 것을 보고 저도 따라 해 보기로 했어요.
dialogue.romanization: chinguga maeil geonneun geoseul bogo jeodo ttara hae bogiro haesseoyo.
dialogue.en: After seeing my friend walk every day, I decided to try following along too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 자기 전에 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이는 것도 목표예요.
dialogue.romanization: jagi jeone hyudaepon boneun geoseul jurineun geotdo mokpyoyeyo.
dialogue.en: Reducing phone-watching before sleeping is also my goal.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 단어를 외우기 전에 예문을 듣는 게 더 도움이 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: daneoreul oeugi jeone yemuneul deunneun ge deo doumi dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: Listening to example sentences before memorizing words helps more.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write two -기 sentences for tasks or fixed frames, two -는 것 sentences for observed habits, and one 기로 했어요 decision.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say one habit with -기 and one concrete action with -는 것.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives an action such as 먹다, 듣다, 걷다, or 외우다. Decide whether the sentence needs -기, -는 것, 기 전에, 기 위해, or 기로 했어요.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 운동하기는 어렵다, 친구가 운동하는 것을 봤다, and 운동하기로 했다 use different nominalized forms?

beginnerGuide.title: Use -기 for activity labels
beginnerGuide.body: 운동하기, 공부하기, 걷기 can name an activity as a task, goal, or habit plan. This form is common before 어렵다, 쉽다, 전에, 위해, 시작하다, and 기로 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -는 것 for a concrete action
beginnerGuide.body: 친구가 걷는 것을 봤어요 and 매일 늦게 먹는 것을 줄이고 있어요 point to an action you see, know, feel, or treat as a concrete habit.

beginnerGuide.title: Memorize the fixed frames
beginnerGuide.body: 기로 했어요, 기 전에, 기 위해서, and 기 시작하다 do not freely switch to -는 것. Learn them as full chunks.

checkpoints: I can use -기 for activities, goals, difficulty, and fixed forms.
I can use -는 것/거 for a specific action, fact, or event.
I can keep fixed expressions like -기로 했어요 and -기 전에.

curriculumTrack.label: B2 Advanced Control
curriculumTrack.description: Causatives, counterfactuals, nominalisation, attitude endings, discourse control, and register switching.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Turn actions into nouns without making the sentence heavy.
exitTask.prompt: Say one habit with -기 and one concrete action with -는 것.

sampleAnswer.ko: 매일 듣기가 어려워요. 그래도 문장을 따라 말하는 것이 도움이 돼요.
sampleAnswer.en: Listening every day is hard. Still, repeating sentences helps.

checklist: I can use -기 for activities, goals, difficulty, and fixed forms.
I can use -는 것/거 for a specific action, fact, or event.
I can keep fixed expressions like -기로 했어요 and -기 전에.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: You want to talk about exercising, studying, listening, memorizing, and cutting down on phone time. Korean makes you choose whether the action is an activity label, a concrete observed action, or part of a fixed grammar frame.
objectives: Choose -기 for activity labels, goals, and fixed frames such as 기로 했어요, 기 전에, 기 위해, and 기 시작하다.
Choose -는 것 or spoken -는 거 for concrete actions, habits, and things you see, know, feel, describe, or reduce.
Practice the contrast with useful habit and study verbs: 운동하다, 걷다, 듣다, 읽다, 외우다, 배우다, 자다, 먹다, 쉬다, and 줄이다.
hook.whyItMatters: English uses one -ing shape for many jobs. Korean splits those jobs. 운동하기는 어렵다, 운동하는 것을 봤다, and 운동하기로 했다 are not interchangeable, because each sentence treats the action differently.

grammarNotes.title: V-기 — turning a verb into a noun
grammarNotes.func: Add 기 to a verb stem to name the action as a thing. The 기-noun can be a task, a goal, or the object of verbs like 좋아하다, 싫어하다, 시작하다, and it is the natural subject of difficulty/ease adjectives like 어렵다, 쉽다, 힘들다.

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㄹ (ㄹ stays before 기)
As the object of 좋아하다/싫어하다 etc.

examples.en: I like reading books.
examples.note: 읽기 names the action so it can be the object of 좋아하다.

examples.en: Today's homework is writing a diary.
examples.note: 쓰기 is a plain noun (a task/title) here, right after 은.

examples.en: Speaking Korean is the hardest.
examples.note: 말하기 is the subject (with 가) of 어렵다 — a very common skill-label use.

examples.en: Getting up early is hard for me.
examples.note: Adjectives of difficulty/ease (힘들다, 쉽다, 좋다) naturally take a V-기 subject.

keyPoint.label: When to reach for V-기
keyPoint.body: Use V-기 to label an action as a thing — especially as the subject of 어렵다/쉽다/좋다/힘들다, or the object of 좋아하다/싫어하다/시작하다. It sounds abstract and title-like, which is exactly why textbook section headings are 듣기, 읽기, 쓰기, 말하기.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: After a stem ending in a plain consonant, the 기 tenses: 읽기 [일끼], 먹기 [먹끼], 닦기 [닥끼]. Vowel stems stay soft: 가기 [가기], 자기 [자기].

drill.instruction: Add 기 to the bracketed verb and choose 를 or 가 so the sentence works.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'reading' can be a noun on its own, but Korean cannot use the dictionary form 읽다 as a noun. Nominalise the stem first: 읽 + 기 → 읽기, then add the particle.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 것/거 — an action or fact as a noun
grammarNotes.func: Add 는 것 (casual 는 거) to a verb to name an action, a habit, or something you saw or know — as a noun. It points at the real, ongoing act, and it is the everyday default after 좋아하다 and as a sentence subject.

formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹는 것, 보다 → 보는 것

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㄹ (ㄹ drops before 는)
formTable.ex: 살다 → 사는 것, 만들다 → 만드는 것

examples.en: I like watching movies.
examples.note: 보는 것 names the activity of watching — sounds more everyday than 보기.

examples.en: Waiting for a friend is boring.
examples.note: 것이 contracts to 게 in speech; here it is the subject of 지루하다.

examples.en: Exercising every day is important.
examples.note: 는 것 carries the habit (every day), which 기 cannot do as smoothly.

examples.ko: 동생이 몰래 과자 먹는 걸 봤어요.
examples.romanization: dong-saeng-i mol-lae gwa-ja meog-neun geol bwass-eo-yo.
examples.en: I saw my younger sibling secretly eating snacks.
examples.note: 는 것 names an action you witnessed; 걸 = 것을 in speech.

keyPoint.label: 기 vs 는 것
keyPoint.body: Both make a verb into a noun. V-기 is abstract and title-like — good for skills, tasks, and subjects of 어렵다/쉽다 (말하기가 어려워요). V-는 것 points at the real act or a habit, and is the default after 좋아하다 and as a subject (영화 보는 게 좋아요). When you are talking and unsure, 는 거 is the safer choice.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 것 links its final ㅅ into a following vowel: 것을 [거슬], 것이 [거시]. In casual speech learn the contractions early — 것이 → 게 [게], 것을 → 걸 [걸], 것은 → 건 [건] — they are everywhere.

drill.instruction: Rewrite with V-는 거 and the right contracted particle (게 for subject, 걸 for object).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners often drop 는 and glue 것 straight onto the stem. The verb must take its present modifier ending -는 before 것: 보 + 는 + 것. Without 는, the phrase is ungrammatical.

grammarNotes.title: V-기로 했어요 — decided to do
grammarNotes.func: Use V-기로 하다 for a decision, plan, or agreement to do something. The 기-noun takes 로 ('settle on') plus 하다. It is almost always said in the past — 했어요 — because the decision is already made by the time you mention it.

formTable.add: 안 + V / V-지 않 + 기로 했어요

examples.en: I've decided to get up early from tomorrow.
examples.note: Personal resolution; past 했어요 even though the action is in the future.

examples.en: We decided to go hiking together on the weekend.
examples.note: 우리 + 같이 makes it a mutual agreement, not a solo decision.

examples.en: I've decided not to drink coffee at night.
examples.note: The negative 안 goes before the verb, not after 기로.

examples.en: I've decided to rest at home today.
examples.note: 쉬기 nominalised, then 로 했어요 for the decision.

keyPoint.label: 했어요 vs 해요
keyPoint.body: The decision is usually reported in the past: V-기로 했어요 ('I (have) decided'), because the decision already exists by the time you say it. Use the present V-기로 해요 / 할게요 only when you are making the resolution at the very moment of speaking ('okay, I'll do X from now on').

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 기로 is read smoothly [기로], with no special change. A tensing stem still tenses the 기: 먹기로 [먹끼로]; and ㅎ + ㄱ aspirates: 끊기로 [끈키로].

drill.instruction: Turn each plan into a decision with V-기로 했어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: The pattern needs the particle 로 ('settle on'), not the object particle 를. 기 + 로 + 하다 is a fixed chunk meaning 'decide to'; 기를 하다 is not a decision and sounds wrong.

grammarNotes.title: V-기 위해(서) — in order to do
grammarNotes.func: Use V-기 위해(서) to give the purpose of an action: 'in order to V'. The verb is nominalised with 기, then 위해(서) ('for the sake of') marks it as the goal. For a noun goal, use N을/를 위해(서) with no 기.

examples.en: I exercise every day in order to get healthy.
examples.note: Purpose comes first; the main action (운동해요) follows.

examples.en: I study hard in order to pass the exam.
examples.note: The classic goal-then-effort pattern.

examples.en: I'm learning Korean in order to work in Korea.
examples.note: 서 dropped here; the meaning is the same, just a little more formal.

examples.en: I work hard for my family.
examples.note: Noun version: N + 을 위해서, with no 기 because the goal is already a noun.

keyPoint.label: V-기 위해서 vs V-(으)려고
keyPoint.body: Both mean 'in order to'. 기 위해서 states a deliberate, often weighty goal and works in writing and speech (시험에 합격하기 위해서 공부해요). V-(으)려고 is lighter and conversational. For a noun goal there is no 기 — you must use N을/를 위해서 (건강을 위해서).

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 위해서 [위해서]; the formal 위하여 [위하여]. The 기 still tenses after a plain-consonant stem: 먹기 위해 [먹끼 위해].

drill.instruction: Join the goal and the action with V-기 위해서 (or N을/를 위해서 for a noun goal).
drill.model: [살을 빼다] / 매일 운동해요 → 살을 빼기 위해서 매일 운동해요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: A verb before 위해서 must be nominalised: 배우 + 기 → 배우기 위해서. You cannot put the dictionary form 배우다 straight in front of 위해서.

grammarNotes.title: V-기 전에 — before doing
grammarNotes.func: Use V-기 전에 to say one action happens before another: 'before V-ing'. The verb takes 기, then 전에 ('before') follows. The tense lives only in the main clause, never on the verb before 전에.

formTable.ex: 자다 → 자기 전에, 먹다 → 먹기 전에

formTable.when: Tense stays on the main verb

examples.ko: 자기 전에 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: ja-gi jeon-e hyu-dae-pon bo-neun geos-eul ju-ri-gi-ro haess-eo-yo.
examples.en: I decided to cut down on looking at my phone before sleeping.
examples.note: 자기 전에 is fixed with 기; 보는 것 is the habit being reduced.

examples.en: I wash my hands before eating.
examples.note: An everyday routine sentence; tense is on the main verb 씻어요.

examples.ko: 단어를 외우기 전에 예문을 먼저 들어요.
examples.romanization: dan-eo-reul oe-u-gi jeon-e ye-mun-eul meon-jeo deul-eo-yo.
examples.en: Before memorizing words, I listen to example sentences first.
examples.note: 외우기 전에 is far more natural than trying to use 외우는 것 here.

examples.ko: 말하기 전에 한 번 더 생각해요.
examples.romanization: mal-ha-gi jeon-e han beon deo saeng-gak-hae-yo.
examples.en: Before speaking, I think one more time.
examples.note: A handy social-habit sentence.

keyPoint.label: 기 전에 vs N 전에
keyPoint.body: Before a verb, you need 기: 먹기 전에, 자기 전에. Before a plain noun, there is no 기 — just add 전에: 수업 전에, 점심 전에, 운동 전에. And the opposite of 전에 is 후에 / -(으)ㄴ 후에 (after doing): 먹은 후에.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 전에 [저네] in fast speech, as the ㄴ links to the next vowel. The 기 still tenses after a plain-consonant stem: 먹기 전에 [먹끼 저네].

drill.instruction: Complete each sentence with V-기 전에 using the bracketed verb.
drill.model: [자다] 이를 닦아요. → 자기 전에 이를 닦아요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not put past tense on the verb before 전에. The verb before 전에 stays as plain 기 (먹기 전에); the past meaning goes on the main verb (씻었어요).

grammarNotes.title: V-기 시작하다 — start doing
grammarNotes.func: Use V-기 시작하다 to say you start an action. 시작하다 ('start') can take a plain noun object (운동을 시작하다), but when the thing you start is a verb, you nominalise it with 기 first. The tense goes on 시작하다.

formTable.ex: 듣다 → 듣기 시작하다, 읽다 → 읽기 시작하다

examples.en: I started listening to Korean news little by little.
examples.note: 듣다 becomes 듣기 before 시작하다; the past tense is on 시작했어요.

examples.ko: 아침에 걷기 시작하니까 잠이 덜 와요.
examples.romanization: a-chim-e geod-gi si-jak-ha-ni-kka jam-i deol wa-yo.
examples.en: Since I started walking in the morning, I feel less sleepy.
examples.note: The whole started action can become a reason with -니까.

examples.ko: 책을 읽기 시작하면 휴대폰을 덜 보게 돼요.
examples.romanization: chaeg-eul ilg-gi si-jak-ha-myeon hyu-dae-pon-eul deol bo-ge dwae-yo.
examples.en: Once I start reading a book, I end up looking at my phone less.
examples.note: 시작하면 turns the start into a condition.

examples.en: I started exercising.
examples.note: 운동 is already a noun, so it takes 을 directly — no 기 needed.

keyPoint.label: 기 시작하다 vs N 시작하다
keyPoint.body: If you start a verb action, nominalise it: 걷기 시작하다, 듣기 시작하다, 읽기 시작하다. If you start a thing that is already a noun, just add 을/를: 운동을 시작하다, 공부를 시작하다. So '운동하다' becomes 운동하기 시작하다 OR 운동을 시작하다 — but never 운동기 시작하다.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: The 기 tenses after a plain-consonant stem: 듣기 [듣끼], 읽기 [일끼], 걷기 [걷끼]. 시작하다 is [시자카다], with ㄱ + ㅎ blending into an aspirated sound.

drill.instruction: Rewrite each into 'started doing' with V-기 시작했어요.
drill.model: 한국 드라마를 보다 → 한국 드라마를 보기 시작했어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not attach 기 to a noun. 운동 is a noun, so use 운동을 시작하다; only the verb 운동하다 can take 기 → 운동하기 시작하다.

exampleSentence.en: Exercising is hard, but it is good for your health.
exampleSentence.note: Use -기 when 운동하다 becomes an activity label.

exampleSentence.en: Before starting exercise, I set a goal.
exampleSentence.note: 운동 is already a noun, so it can take 을 before 시작하다.

exampleSentence.ko: 공부하기 전에 오늘 목표를 먼저 써요.
exampleSentence.en: Before studying, I write today's goal first.
exampleSentence.note: 기 전에 is the natural before-doing frame.

exampleSentence.en: Before starting my studying, I clear my desk.
exampleSentence.note: 공부 is a noun; 공부를 시작하다 is different from 공부하기 시작하다 but both are useful.

exampleSentence.en: I decided to start with walking first.
exampleSentence.note: 걷기 names the activity; 시작하기로 했어요 reports the decision.

exampleSentence.ko: 예문을 듣는 게 단어 외우기에 도움이 돼요.
exampleSentence.en: Listening to example sentences helps with memorizing words.
exampleSentence.note: 듣는 게 presents listening as the concrete helpful action.

exampleSentence.ko: 책을 읽기 시작하면 휴대폰을 덜 보게 돼요.
exampleSentence.en: Once I start reading a book, I end up looking at my phone less.
exampleSentence.note: 읽기 시작하다 is the fixed start-doing frame.

exampleSentence.en: Before memorizing words, I listen to example sentences.
exampleSentence.note: 외우기 전에 is more natural than trying to attach 전에 to 외우는 것.

exampleSentence.en: It has been six months since I started learning Korean.
exampleSentence.note: 배우기 시작하다 marks the beginning of the learning action.

exampleSentence.en: I started with walking.
exampleSentence.note: A noun or -기 activity can come before 시작하다.

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 매일 운동하는 것을 알고 있어요.
exampleSentence.en: I know that my friend exercises every day.
exampleSentence.note: 알다 often takes a concrete proposition with -는 것.

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 걷는 것을 보고 저도 시작했어요.
exampleSentence.en: After seeing my friend walk, I started too.
exampleSentence.note: 보다 makes the action concrete and observable, so -는 것 fits.

exampleSentence.ko: 매일 듣는 것이 발음에 도움이 된다고 느껴요.
exampleSentence.en: I feel that listening every day helps pronunciation.
exampleSentence.note: 느끼다 can take a proposition treated as a concrete fact.

exampleSentence.ko: 자기 전에 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이기로 했어요.
exampleSentence.en: I decided to reduce looking at my phone before sleeping.
exampleSentence.note: 자기 전에 is the fixed before-sleeping frame.

exampleSentence.ko: 밤에 늦게 먹는 것을 줄이려고 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I am trying to reduce eating late at night.
exampleSentence.note: 먹는 것 is the habit being reduced.

exampleSentence.ko: 쉬는 것도 공부 계획에 넣어야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: Resting should also be included in the study plan.
exampleSentence.note: 쉬는 것 points to resting as a concrete part of the plan.

exampleSentence.en: I am building a habit of listening every day.
exampleSentence.note: -는 습관 naturally describes repeated behavior.

exampleSentence.ko: 오늘 목표는 예문 다섯 개를 외우는 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: Today's goal is memorizing five example sentences.
exampleSentence.note: Spoken 거예요 makes the action into the goal.

exampleSentence.en: For my health, I decided to walk every day.
exampleSentence.note: Noun + 을 위해 is the noun version of V-기 위해.

exampleSentence.ko: 꾸준히 듣는 게 말하기에도 도움이 돼요.
exampleSentence.en: Listening consistently helps speaking too.
exampleSentence.note: 꾸준히 works well with repeated -는 것 habits.

extendedVocabulary.english: to reduce, to cut down on

exampleSentence.en: I decided to cut down on looking at my phone.
exampleSentence.note: The thing reduced is a concrete habit, so 보는 것을 is natural.

extendedDialogue.setting: A tutor helps a learner turn vague goals into Korean sentences using -기, -는 것, and fixed nominalized frames.

lines.speaker: 튜터
lines.ko: 매일 운동하기는 어렵지만 건강을 위해 필요해요.
lines.romanization: maeil undonghagineun eoryeopjiman geongangeul wihae piryohaeyo.
lines.en: Exercising every day is hard, but it is necessary for health.
lines.grammarNote: 운동하기 names the activity as a task.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: So I decided to start with walking.
lines.grammarNote: 시작하기로 했어요 is a fixed decision frame.

lines.speaker: 튜터
lines.ko: 좋아요. 친구가 매일 걷는 것을 보고 따라 해 보기로 한 거죠?
lines.romanization: joayo. chinguga maeil geonneun geoseul bogo ttara hae bogiro han geojyo?
lines.en: Good. You saw your friend walking every day and decided to try following along, right?
lines.grammarNote: 걷는 것을 is an observed concrete action.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 네. 그리고 자기 전에 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이기로 했어요.
lines.romanization: ne. geurigo jagi jeone hyudaepon boneun geoseul jurigiro haesseoyo.
lines.en: Yes. And I decided to reduce looking at my phone before sleeping.
lines.grammarNote: 자기 전에 uses -기; 보는 것을 is the habit being reduced.

lines.speaker: 튜터
lines.ko: 단어를 외우기 전에 예문을 듣는 것도 좋아요.
lines.romanization: daneoreul oeugi jeone yemuneul deunneun geotdo joayo.
lines.en: Listening to example sentences before memorizing words is also good.
lines.grammarNote: 외우기 전에 is fixed, while 듣는 것 presents a concrete practice.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그럼 오늘 목표는 예문을 먼저 듣고 단어를 외우는 거예요.
lines.romanization: geureom oneul mokpyoneun yemuneul meonjeo deutgo daneoreul oeuneun geoyeyo.
lines.en: Then today's goal is listening to the examples first and memorizing the words.
lines.grammarNote: Spoken 거예요 turns the whole action into the goal.

readingText.title: -기와 -는 것을 고르는 법
readingText.body: 민서는 건강을 위해 운동을 시작하고 싶었지만, 매일 운동하기는 부담스러웠다. 그래서 걷기부터 시작하기로 했다. 친구가 아침마다 걷는 것을 보고 따라 해 보기로 한 것이다. 한국어 공부도 같은 방식으로 바꿨다. 단어를 외우기 전에 예문을 먼저 듣고, 자기 전에 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이기로 했다. 이렇게 말하면 -기는 목표나 순서를 만들고, -는 것은 실제로 보고 줄이고 반복하는 행동을 가리킨다. 민서는 이제 "공부하기"와 "공부하는 것"을 같은 말로 외우지 않고, 문장 안에서 어떤 역할을 하는지 먼저 본다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo wanted to start exercising for her health, but exercising every day felt burdensome. So she decided to start with walking. She saw her friend walking every morning and decided to try following along. She changed her Korean study the same way. Before memorizing words, she listens to examples first, and she decided to reduce looking at her phone before sleeping. In these sentences, -기 makes goals and sequences, while -는 것 points to actions that are seen, reduced, or repeated. Minseo no longer memorizes 공부하기 and 공부하는 것 as the same thing; she first checks what job the action has inside the sentence.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 왜 걷기부터 시작하기로 했어요?
단어를 외우기 전에 무엇을 먼저 해요?
-는 것은 어떤 행동을 가리킨다고 했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 실제로 보고 줄이고 반복하는 행동을 가리킨다고 했어요.

culturalNote.title: 말할 때는 거, 쓸 때는 것
culturalNote.body: In speech, Koreans often shorten 것은 to 건, 것을 to 걸, and 것이 to 게. So 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이기로 했어요 may sound like 휴대폰 보는 걸 줄이기로 했어요. In writing, especially school, work, and proposals, keeping 것 is cleaner. For purpose statements, -기 위해 is common in formal writing: 건강을 지키기 위해, 지출을 줄이기 위해, 목표를 이루기 위해.
culturalNote.tip: When you are unsure, ask what the action is doing in the sentence: task or fixed frame takes -기; concrete action or habit often takes -는 것/거.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses -기 as an activity label?
inlineExercises.explanation: 운동하기 names the activity as a general task.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses -는 것 for a concrete habit being reduced?
inlineExercises.explanation: The habit being reduced is the concrete action 휴대폰 보는 것.

inlineExercises.prompt: Choose the correct fixed decision frame.
inlineExercises.explanation: 기로 했어요 is the standard chunk for a settled decision.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 단어를 ____ 전에 예문을 들어요. (외우다 → before doing)
inlineExercises.explanation: Before doing uses V기 전에, so 외우다 becomes 외우기 전에.

inlineExercises.prompt: 운동___ 시작했어요. (I started exercising.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 시작하다 can take the activity noun as an object, so 운동을 fits. 이 would make exercise the subject.

inlineExercises.prompt: 책을 ___ 단어를 외워요. (읽다 → before doing)
inlineExercises.explanation: V-기 전에 means before doing. 읽다 becomes 읽기 전에.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'I decided to memorize words.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -기로 했어요 is the fixed decision frame. 외우다 becomes 외우기로 before 했어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'I started learning Korean.'
inlineExercises.explanation: V-기 시작하다 means start doing. 배우다 becomes 배우기 before 시작했어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: '한국어를 공부하는 위해서 왔어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: Purpose uses V-기 위해서, not V-는 위해서. 공부하다 becomes 공부하기 위해서.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence treats walking as an activity label?
inlineExercises.explanation: -기 can turn the activity into a topic label. 걷기는 means walking as an activity.

bullets: -기 often names an activity as a task, purpose, sequence, or decision: 운동하기, 외우기 전에, 걷기로 했어요.
-는 것/거 points to a concrete action, habit, or fact: 걷는 것을 봤어요, 보는 것을 줄여요, 듣는 게 도움이 돼요.
Fixed frames do not freely switch forms: 기로 했어요, 기 위해서, 기 전에, and 기 시작하다 stay with -기.
The vocabulary set is tied to the grammar: study actions, health habits, and reduction goals naturally force the -기 vs -는 것 choice.

writingTask.prompt: Write 3 sentences about a new habit: what you decided to do, why (the purpose), and that you've started — turning the actions into nouns.
writingTask.hint: Use V-기로 했어요 for the decision, V-기 위해(서) for the purpose, and V-기 시작했어요 to say you started; name actions with V-기 or V-는 것.
writingTask.model: 저는 매일 아침에 운동하기로 했어요. 건강해지기 위해서 일찍 걷기 시작했어요. 운동하는 것이 생각보다 어렵지 않아요.
writingTask.modelEn: I decided to exercise every morning. To get healthy, I started walking early. Exercising isn't as hard as I thought.

canDo: Name an action as a noun with V-기 (운동하기) and V-는 것 (운동하는 것)
Express a decision or plan with V-기로 했어요 (운동하기로 했어요)
Give the purpose of an action with V-기 위해(서) (건강해지기 위해서)
Say something happens before another action (V-기 전에) and that you start it (V-기 시작하다)

chapters.title: Sentence-Final Attitude Endings
chapters.goal: Add the speaker's reaction at the end of the sentence.
chapters.scenario: You notice something, feel surprise, make a careful prediction, or express regret.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Korean is more fun than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 처음에는 어려울 줄 알았는데 생각보다 괜찮군요.
dialogue.romanization: cheoeumeneun eoryeoul jul aranneunde saenggakboda gwaenchanhgunyo.
dialogue.en: I thought it would be hard at first, but it is better than expected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Oh, they have already arrived.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If you leave now, you will probably be a little late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 어제 시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: eoje sigani isseosseumyeon gachi gasseul tendeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had had time yesterday, I would have gone with you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 연습을 많이 했으니까 잘하는 게 당연하네요.
dialogue.romanization: yeonseubeul mani haesseunikka jalhaneun ge dangyeonhaneyo.
dialogue.en: Since you practiced a lot, no wonder you are good.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one fresh realization with -네요, one formal realization with -군요, one hedged prediction with -ㄹ걸요, and one regret with -았/었을 텐데요.
chapters.realLifeTask: React to one real situation with -네요, -군요, -ㄹ걸요, or -았/었을 텐데요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a fact or situation. Choose whether your response should sound like fresh noticing, formal acknowledgement, hedged prediction, or regret.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 재미있네요, 도착하셨군요, 늦을걸요, and 갔을 텐데요 do not have the same speaker attitude?

beginnerGuide.title: Read the speaker's attitude
beginnerGuide.body: These endings do not just add politeness. They tell the listener whether you just noticed something, are acknowledging new information, are guessing, or are regretting a missed outcome.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate noticing from knowing
beginnerGuide.body: -네요 works when the speaker is freshly realizing something. If you already knew it, a plain statement or -잖아요 may fit better.

beginnerGuide.title: Keep regret and prediction apart
beginnerGuide.body: -ㄹ걸요 can hedge a prediction, while -았/었을 텐데요 looks back at a missed past condition. Do not flatten both into English would/probably.

checkpoints: I can use -네요 for a fresh realization.
I can use -군요 for a stronger or more formal realization.
I can use -ㄹ걸요 for a careful prediction and -았/었을 텐데요 for regret.

curriculumTrack.label: B2 Advanced Control
curriculumTrack.description: Causatives, counterfactuals, nominalisation, attitude endings, discourse control, and register switching.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Add the speaker's reaction at the end of the sentence.
exitTask.prompt: React to one real situation with -네요, -군요, -ㄹ걸요, or -았/었을 텐데요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 생각보다 어렵네요. 어제 조금 더 연습했으면 좋았을 텐데요.
sampleAnswer.en: It is harder than I expected. It would have been nice if I had practiced a little more yesterday.

checklist: I can use -네요 for a fresh realization.
I can use -군요 for a stronger or more formal realization.
I can use -ㄹ걸요 for a careful prediction and -았/었을 텐데요 for regret.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: You are reacting in real time: Korean feels more fun than expected, someone has already arrived, a friend may be late, and a missed plan still feels disappointing. The grammar is in the ending because the ending tells the listener how you are taking the information.
objectives: Use -네요 for fresh realization from what you just noticed.
Use -군요/-구나 for stronger acknowledgement or exclamation.
Use -(으)ㄹ걸요 for a softened prediction and -았/었을 텐데요 for regret or unfulfilled expectation.
hook.whyItMatters: A plain statement reports information. These endings report your stance toward the information. 재미있어요, 재미있네요, and 재미있군요 can describe the same fact, but they do not sound like the same reaction.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-네요: realizing or noticing something right now
grammarNotes.func: -네요 is the on-the-spot reaction ending. You attach it when you discover, see, hear, taste, or otherwise newly notice something at the moment of speaking. It carries a light feeling of mild surprise or fresh awareness: "Oh, it's ...!" Use it when the information just hit you, not when you are reporting a fact you already knew.

examples.en: Oh, it's raining outside.
examples.note: You just looked out and noticed the rain now -- that fresh discovery is exactly what -네요 marks.

examples.en: Wow, this kimchi stew is really delicious!
examples.note: Said after the first bite -- a reaction to something you are experiencing at this moment.

examples.en: It's already 6. Time flies.
examples.note: Noticing the clock and the speed of time on the spot; 빠르네요 reacts to a realization, not a stored fact.

examples.en: You really speak Korean well!
examples.note: A natural compliment -- you just heard them speak and are reacting, which is why -네요 sounds warm here.

keyPoint.label: -네요 = reacting to NEW information
keyPoint.body: The core trigger is newness to the speaker. If you already knew the fact and are just stating it, use plain -아/어요. The moment of fresh noticing is what makes -네요 the right choice.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: Past tense -았네요/-었네요 has the ㅅ assimilate to ㄴ: 끝났네요 sounds like [끈난네요], 갔네요 like [간네요]. Learners who pronounce a clear [ㅅ] here sound non-native.

drill.instruction: React in the moment using A/V-네요. Fill in the blank with the verb/adjective in parentheses.
items: 여기 사람이 많이 (있다) -> 여기 사람이 많이 ____.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 어제 비가 왔네요. (to report yesterday's weather you already knew)
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 어제 비가 왔어요. / (noticing puddles now) 비가 왔네요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers reach for -네요 whenever something feels noteworthy, but it must mark information that is new to you at the moment of speaking. Reporting a fact you already knew takes plain -아/어요; -네요 only fits when you are noticing it fresh.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-군요 / -구나: "I see, so that's how it is"
grammarNotes.func: -군요 (polite) and -구나 (casual) express the moment of understanding: you take in new information and acknowledge it, often realizing the reason or background behind something. Where -네요 is a gut reaction to what you perceive, -군요/-구나 is the click of comprehension -- "Ah, so THAT'S why / so it's like that."

formTable.ex: 가다 -> 가는군요 / 가는구나 (I see, you're going)
아프다 -> 아팠군요 / 아팠구나 (Ah, you were sick)
동생이군요 / 동생이구나 (Oh, it's your younger sibling)

examples.en: Ah, so that's why you couldn't come yesterday.
examples.note: 그래서 + -군요 is the classic pairing: you just grasped the reason behind something.

examples.en: So THIS is that famous restaurant.
examples.note: You connect what you heard before with what you now see -- a moment of recognition, not just surprise.

examples.en: I see, so Minsu is good at cooking.
examples.note: Verb 잘하다 takes -는군요 in the present; you are registering a newly learned fact about Minsu.

examples.en: Oh, you already graduated. Time really flies.
examples.note: Casual -구나 to a close friend; it shows you absorbing news and reflecting on it.

keyPoint.label: Verbs need -는군요 in the present
keyPoint.body: Adjectives and nouns attach -군요 directly (춥군요, 학생이군요), but present-tense verbs insert -는-: 가는군요, 먹는군요. Past tense is uniform for both: -았/었군요. -구나 is simply the casual (반말) version.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: -는군요 links the final ㄴ into the 요 in fast speech, sounding like [는군뇨]. The casual -구나 is often drawn out for feeling: 그렇구나~, signaling a thoughtful "ahh, I see."

drill.instruction: Show that you just understood something using -군요 (polite) or -구나 (casual).
items: (그래서 전화를 안 받았다) -> 그래서 전화를 안 ____.
(이 노래를 직접 만들었다) -> 이 노래를 직접 ____.
(casual: 너도 이 영화 봤다) -> 너도 이 영화 ____.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers attach -군요 straight to every stem because adjectives work that way (춥군요). But present-tense verbs require the inserted -는-: 잘하다 -> 잘하는군요, 먹다 -> 먹는군요. Forgetting -는- is the single most common mistake with this ending.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-(으)ㄹ걸요: "probably," a soft guess
grammarNotes.func: -(으)ㄹ걸요 offers a tentative guess based on your own reasoning or hunch, softened so it doesn't sound too sure. It means "I think probably ..." or "it's likely that ...," and is common when answering someone gently without claiming certainty. (Written the same, -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 with a sighing tone means regret, "I should have ...," but here we focus on the guessing use.)

examples.en: The shop is probably closed now.
examples.note: A soft prediction about a present situation; -았을걸요 guesses the door is already in a closed state.

examples.ko: 민지 씨는 매운 거 잘 먹을걸요.
examples.romanization: minji ssineun maeun geo jal meogeulgeoryo.
examples.en: Minji can probably handle spicy food well.
examples.note: You're guessing from what you know of her -- not stating a fact, just a confident-but-soft hunch.

examples.en: That movie has probably already ended.
examples.note: Past-guess -았을걸요 estimates about something completed; very natural in casual conversation.

examples.en: Since it's the weekend, the roads will probably be jammed.
examples.note: Reasoning from a known cause (주말이라서) to a likely outcome -- the textbook use of a soft guess.

keyPoint.label: -(으)ㄹ걸요 = your guess, not shared knowledge
keyPoint.body: Use -(으)ㄹ걸요 when the conclusion comes from your own inference and you want to stay humble about it. Compare -(으)ㄹ 거예요, which sounds more confident/declarative. -걸요 always softens, as if to say "I'm fairly sure, but don't quote me."

grammarNotes.pronunciation: The 걸 is tensed to [껄]: 올걸요 sounds like [올껄요], 먹을걸요 like [머글껄요]. The sentence also rises slightly at the end, giving it its tentative, musing feel.

drill.instruction: Answer with a soft guess using V/A-(으)ㄹ걸요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 내일 비가 올 거예요. (when you only have a vague hunch, not real evidence)
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 내일 비가 올걸요. (a soft, unsure guess) -- use 올 거예요 only when you're genuinely confident.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English "probably" and "will" feel interchangeable, so learners default to -(으)ㄹ 거예요 even for hunches. But -(으)ㄹ 거예요 sounds like a confident claim, while -(으)ㄹ걸요 keeps it hedged. Match the ending to how sure you actually are. Also keep -(으)ㄹ걸요 (guess) separate from -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 (regret, "I should have").

grammarNotes.title: V-았/었을 텐데(요): "it would have ..., but"
grammarNotes.func: -았/었을 텐데(요) expresses a confident guess about an unrealized past -- what surely would have happened -- usually paired with a contrasting reality, regret, or concern. It looks back and supposes: "It would have been ... (but it wasn't / but something got in the way)." The 텐데 leaves the thought hanging, inviting sympathy or a soft follow-up rather than a blunt complaint.

formTable.ex: 오다 -> 왔을 텐데요 (They would have come)
시간이 있었으면 갔을 텐데요 (If I'd had time, I'd have gone)
쉽다 -> 쉬웠을 텐데요 (It would have been easy)
바쁘다 -> 바쁠 텐데요 (They must be busy, though)

examples.ko: 어제 시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: eoje sigani isseosseumyeon gachi gasseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I'd had time yesterday, I would have gone with you.
examples.note: The trip didn't happen; -았/었을 텐데요 keeps the regret soft instead of stating a flat "I couldn't go."

examples.en: If I'd known in advance, I would have helped.
examples.note: Polite regret after missing a chance to help -- 미리 알았으면 sets the unreal condition.

examples.ko: 조금만 일찍 왔으면 표를 살 수 있었을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: jogeumman iljjik wasseumyeon pyoreul sal su isseosseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If you'd come just a bit earlier, you could have bought a ticket.
examples.note: Gentle 'too bad' about a missed chance; the 텐데 trails off, softening it.

examples.en: If you'd taken the bus, you wouldn't have been late.
examples.note: Looking back at what would have avoided the problem -- sympathetic, not accusatory.

keyPoint.label: Past -았/었을 텐데 = unreal past; present -(으)ㄹ 텐데 = current concern
keyPoint.body: Add the past -았/었- when you're supposing about something that did NOT happen (regret): 갔을 텐데요. Drop it for a present/future worry or contrast: 지금 바쁠 텐데요 ("they must be busy right now, though"). Mixing these changes the meaning from regret to ongoing concern.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 텐데 is [텐데] with a clear, even tone, but the sentence-final 요 trails off and drops in pitch -- that falling, unfinished melody is what signals the lingering 'but...' feeling. Don't end it sharply.

drill.instruction: Express soft regret about an unreal past using -았/었으면 ... -았/었을 텐데요.
drill.model: (시간 / 같이 가다) -> 시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요.
items: (연습 많이 하다 / 쉽다) -> 연습을 많이 했으면 훨씬 ____.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 시간이 있으면 같이 갔을 텐데요. (present 있으면 with a past-regret result)
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: For regret about the past, the IF-clause must also be past-unreal: 있었으면, not 있으면. English "if I had time" hides the tense, so learners use present 있으면 and clash with the past 갔을 텐데요. Match both halves to the unreal past: 있었으면 ... 갔을 텐데요.

grammarNotes.title: -군요 vs -네요: both react, but not the same way
grammarNotes.func: -네요 and -군요 both respond to new information, but with a different feel. -네요 is an immediate, conversational gut reaction to what you directly perceive right now ("oh, look at that"). -군요 is a slightly more composed acknowledgement -- you take in a fact or explanation and register it ("I see, so that's the case"). Knowing which one to reach for keeps your reactions sounding natural.

formTable.when: Acknowledging a fact/explanation you just learned

formTable.ex: 그래서 못 왔군요 (So that's why you couldn't come)

examples.en: Oh, it's snowing!
examples.note: -네요: a spontaneous reaction to what you see out the window this second.

examples.en: Ah, so that's why you were late.
examples.note: -군요: you take in the explanation and acknowledge the reason -- calmer than a gut reaction.

examples.en: I see. I had it wrong.
examples.note: Both in one breath: 군요 accepts the new fact, 네요 marks your own fresh realization about yourself.

examples.en: The coffee here is really good.
examples.note: -네요: a direct, in-the-moment reaction to taste -- 맛있군요 would sound oddly stiff here.

keyPoint.label: Perceiving now -> -네요; registering a fact -> -군요
keyPoint.body: If you're reacting to something you directly sense at this moment (taste, weather, someone's arrival), -네요 sounds warm and natural. If you're acknowledging information or a reason that just clicked, -군요 fits. -군요 can sound stiff for simple sensory reactions, and -네요 can sound under-reactive for absorbing a full explanation.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 그렇군요 is pronounced [그러쿠뇨] (ㅎ + ㄱ tenses/aspirates to ㅋ), and 그렇네요 is [그런네요] (ㅎ assimilates to ㄴ before ㄴ). Both are extremely common backchannels -- saying them clearly helps you sound like an engaged listener.

drill.instruction: Choose -네요 (direct noticing) or -군요 (acknowledging a fact/reason), then fill the blank.
drill.model: (친구 설명을 듣고) 아, 그래서 그랬____. -> 그랬군요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: For a direct, in-the-moment sensory reaction (taste, weather, a view), Korean prefers -네요; -군요 sounds too composed or bookish there. Learners over-use -군요 because it's taught as "I see," but reserve it for acknowledging facts or reasons, not for spontaneous "wow, this is good!" reactions.

exampleSentence.en: Korean is more fun than I expected.
exampleSentence.note: Fresh realization with -네요.

exampleSentence.en: It is not as hard as I thought.
exampleSentence.note: This word naturally triggers realization endings because expectation changed.

exampleSentence.ko: 처음에는 어려울 줄 알았는데 생각보다 괜찮군요.
exampleSentence.en: I thought it would be hard at first, but it is better than expected.
exampleSentence.note: 어려울 줄 알았다 sets the old expectation.

exampleSentence.en: Oh, they have already arrived.
exampleSentence.note: 벌써 pairs well with surprise or realization.

exampleSentence.en: Oh, they have already arrived.
exampleSentence.note: Past honorific 도착하셨군요 fits polite acknowledgement.

exampleSentence.en: If you leave now, you will probably be a little late.
exampleSentence.note: 늦을걸요 is a softened prediction.

exampleSentence.en: If I had had time, I would have gone with you.
exampleSentence.note: 시간이 있었으면 creates the missed condition.

exampleSentence.en: I would have gone together with you.
exampleSentence.note: 같이 makes the regret relational, not just logistical.

exampleSentence.en: They probably already know.
exampleSentence.note: 이미 often appears in hedged assertions.

exampleSentence.en: There are more people than expected.
exampleSentence.note: A changed expectation naturally takes -네요.

exampleSentence.en: It probably is not certain yet.
exampleSentence.note: -ㄹ걸요 softens a cautious assertion.

exampleSentence.en: If I had said it clearly, there would have been no misunderstanding.
exampleSentence.note: 분명히 sharpens the missed action in a regret sentence.

extendedVocabulary.english: to be natural, obvious, no wonder

exampleSentence.ko: 연습을 많이 했으니까 잘하는 게 당연하네요.
exampleSentence.en: Since you practiced a lot, no wonder you are good.
exampleSentence.note: -네요 makes the comment a realization, not a dismissive judgment.

exampleSentence.en: That must have been really hard for you.
exampleSentence.note: -군요 can acknowledge someone else's experience with empathy.

exampleSentence.en: They probably already know.
exampleSentence.note: 알고 있을걸요 is a common hedged assertion.

exampleSentence.en: I see. I did not know that.
exampleSentence.note: 군요 accepts the fact; 네요 marks the speaker's realization.

extendedDialogue.setting: Friends react to a class, a late schedule, and a missed chance while choosing endings that match their stance.

readingText.title: 끝 어미가 태도를 바꾼다
readingText.body: 민서는 첫 수업을 듣고 "생각보다 재미있네요"라고 말했다. 방금 느낀 놀라움이라서 -네요가 자연스러웠다. 지훈은 설명을 듣고 "그렇군요"라고 했다. 새 정보를 받아들이는 조금 더 차분한 반응이었다. 수업이 끝난 뒤 선생님이 이미 도착한 것을 보고 민서는 "벌써 도착하셨네요"라고 했고, 지훈은 시간을 보더니 "지금 출발하면 늦을걸요"라고 했다. 나중에 민서는 약속에 가지 못한 일을 떠올리며 "시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요"라고 말했다. 같은 사실도 끝 어미가 달라지면 놀람, 인정, 예측, 아쉬움이 서로 다르게 들린다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: After the first class, Minseo said, "It is more fun than I expected." Because it was a surprise she had just felt, -네요 was natural. Jihoon listened to an explanation and said, "I see." That was a calmer acknowledgement of new information. After class, Minseo saw that the teacher had already arrived and said, "Oh, the teacher has already arrived." Jihoon looked at the time and said, "If we leave now, we will probably be late." Later, Minseo remembered not being able to go to an appointment and said, "If I had had time, I would have gone with you." Even with the same facts, the final ending changes whether the sentence sounds like surprise, acknowledgement, prediction, or regret.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 첫 수업 뒤에 어떤 어미를 사용했어요?
지훈이 "늦을걸요"라고 한 이유는 무엇이에요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 지금 출발하면 늦을 것 같다고 부드럽게 예측했기 때문이에요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: -았/었을 텐데요는 어떤 느낌을 나타냈어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 과거에 이루어지지 않은 일에 대한 아쉬움이나 후회를 나타냈어요.

culturalNote.title: 끝 어미는 목소리의 표정
culturalNote.body: In Korean, the final ending often carries the social expression that English might put in intonation. 재미있어요 reports a fact. 재미있네요 shares a fresh reaction. 재미있군요 sounds like a more formal acknowledgement. 늦을걸요 warns softly without sounding bossy. 갔을 텐데요 lets regret trail off instead of making a heavy complaint.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing the ending, ask: am I noticing, acknowledging, guessing, or regretting?

inlineExercises.prompt: Which ending fits a fresh realization after trying Korean class?
inlineExercises.explanation: -네요 marks fresh realization.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is a softened prediction?
inlineExercises.explanation: -ㄹ걸요 gives a hedged assertion or prediction.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence expresses regret about a missed past condition?
inlineExercises.explanation: -았/었으면 ... -았/었을 텐데요 frames an unreal past.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete the acknowledgement: 아, 그런 이유였____. (use -군요)
inlineExercises.explanation: 그런 이유였군요 politely acknowledges a newly understood reason.

inlineExercises.prompt: 생각___ 더 재미있네요. (It is more fun than I expected.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 생각보다 means compared with what I thought or expected. -네요 then reacts to the fresh realization.

inlineExercises.prompt: 이 문법이 생각보다 ___ . (어렵다 → fresh realization)
inlineExercises.explanation: -네요 marks something you notice now. 어렵다 becomes 어렵네요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'Oh, they already arrived.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -군요 acknowledges or takes in information with a stronger “I see” feeling. 벌써 adds the surprise that it already happened.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the regret: '같이 갔으면 좋겠어요.' (missed past plan)
inlineExercises.explanation: For regret about a missed past plan, the result needs past hypothetical language. 좋았을 텐데요 expresses the unfulfilled expectation.

inlineExercises.prompt: You just tried the class and are surprised it is fun. Which fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: -네요 fits fresh realization from direct experience. -ㄹ걸요 is a guess, and -었을 텐데요 is regret/hypothetical.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete the soft guess: 지금 출발하면 아마 안 늦___. (use -(으)ㄹ걸요)
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ걸요 gives a soft, unconfirmed guess. 늦다 ends in the consonant ㅈ, so it takes 을걸요: 안 늦을걸요.

bullets: -네요 marks a fresh realization: 생각보다 재미있네요, 벌써 도착하셨네요.
-군요/-구나 marks stronger acknowledgement or exclamation: 그렇군요, 알고 있었구나.
-(으)ㄹ걸요 softens a prediction or assertion: 늦을걸요, 이미 알고 있을걸요.
-았/었을 텐데요 looks back at an unfulfilled past expectation: 같이 갔을 텐데요.

writingTask.prompt: A friend just arrived and you notice the time. Send a 3-line reaction: react to something you just noticed, show you now understand why, and add a soft guess.
writingTask.hint: Use A/V-네요 for an on-the-spot reaction, A/V-군요 for 'I see,' and -(으)ㄹ걸요 for a soft guess.
writingTask.model: 벌써 도착했네요! 길이 안 막혔군요. 지금 가면 안 늦을걸요.
writingTask.modelEn: Oh, you've arrived already! I see, the road wasn't jammed. If we go now, we probably won't be late.

canDo: React to something noticed right now with A/V-네요 (벌써 도착했네요)
Acknowledge newly understood information with A/V-군요 / -구나 (안 막혔군요)
Offer a soft, reasoned guess with V/A-(으)ㄹ걸요 (안 늦을걸요)
Suppose about an unrealized past with V-았/었을 텐데(요) (늦었을 텐데요)

chapters.title: Topic vs Subject — 은/는 and 이/가
chapters.goal: Choose 은/는 or 이/가 based on what the listener needs to notice.
chapters.scenario: You introduce new information, continue a topic, or contrast two people or things.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: A friend called.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Does that friend call often?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 아니요. 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
dialogue.romanization: aniyo. pyeongsoeneun mesijireul bonaeneunde oneureun jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
dialogue.en: No. Usually they send messages, but today I contacted them first.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Who contacted them first?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 제가 먼저 연락했어요. 질문은 쉬웠는데 대답이 어려웠어요.
dialogue.romanization: jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo. jilmuneun swiwonneunde daedabi eoryeowosseoyo.
dialogue.en: I contacted them first. The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그럼 이 문제는 이유가 제일 중요하네요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom i munjeneun iyuga jeil jungyohaneyo.
dialogue.en: Then for this issue, the reason is the most important thing.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one sentence that introduces new information with 이/가, one that continues a topic with 은/는, one contrast sentence, and one topic-plus-subject sentence.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one real message or event using both 은/는 and 이/가.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 누가?, 무엇이?, or 그 사람은? Answer with 이/가 for focused answers and 은/는 for topic or contrast.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 친구가 전화했어요, 그 친구는 자주 전화해요, and 제가 먼저 연락했어요 use different particles?

beginnerGuide.title: New or focused information
beginnerGuide.body: Use 이/가 when the sentence answers who or what, introduces a subject, or points to exactly one answer: 친구가 전화했어요, 제가 먼저 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Topic and contrast
