beginnerGuide.body: Use 은/는 when the noun is already the topic or when you are contrasting: 그 친구는..., 메시지는 보내지만 전화는 안 해요.

beginnerGuide.title: Frame plus new subject
beginnerGuide.body: Korean can use both in one sentence: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요. The topic is the frame; 이/가 introduces the important subject inside that frame.

checkpoints: I can use 이/가 for new or focused information.
I can use 은/는 for topic, contrast, or continuation.
I can build sentences like 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.

curriculumTrack.label: B2 Advanced Control
curriculumTrack.description: Causatives, counterfactuals, nominalisation, attitude endings, discourse control, and register switching.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Choose 은/는 or 이/가 based on what the listener needs to notice.
exitTask.prompt: Describe one real message or event using both 은/는 and 이/가.

sampleAnswer.ko: 친구가 연락했어요. 그 친구는 보통 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 전화했어요.
sampleAnswer.en: A friend contacted me. That friend usually sends messages, but today they called.

checklist: I can use 이/가 for new or focused information.
I can use 은/는 for topic, contrast, or continuation.
I can build sentences like 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: A friend calls, the topic shifts to that friend, then the speaker contrasts messages with calls and answers who acted first. This chapter is about how Korean particles manage the flow of information.
objectives: Use 이/가 for new information, focused answers, and existence predicates.
Use 은/는 for topic continuity, contrast, and framing.
Build topic-plus-subject sentences such as 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.
hook.whyItMatters: English often uses word order or stress for information flow. Korean marks that flow with particles. 친구가 전화했어요 and 친구는 전화했어요 do not simply mean the same thing with different decoration.

grammarNotes.title: 이/가 — a new or focused subject (new information)
grammarNotes.func: The subject marker 이/가 spotlights WHO or WHAT does or is something. Use it when the subject is new to the conversation, when it answers a 'who?'/'what?' question, or when you want the listener's attention on that exact element. It introduces; it does not assume.

formTable.when: subject noun ends in a consonant
subject noun ends in a vowel

examples.en: It's raining.
examples.note: 비 is brand-new on the scene, so 가 (not 는) presents it as fresh news.

examples.en: Who teaches Korean?
examples.note: The question word 누가 is the focus, so the subject naturally takes 가.

examples.en: My friend lives in Busan.
examples.note: Introducing the friend for the first time, so 가 presents the new subject.

examples.en: There's a problem.
examples.note: Existence sentences with 있다/없다 present new info, so the thing takes 이/가.

keyPoint.label: 이/가 = new and in focus
keyPoint.body: Compare 누가 왔어요? — 친구가 왔어요 (NEW: 가) with 친구는 언제 와요? (already-known friend: 는). 이/가 answers 'who/what'; 은/는 talks ABOUT a known thing.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 이 after a consonant links smoothly: 선생님이 sounds like 선생니미; 책이 like 채기. The final consonant slides onto 이.

drill.instruction: Fill the blank with 이 or 가 to mark the new/focused subject.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English has no topic/subject split, so learners default to one marker for everything. Brand-new, on-the-scene information (weather, sudden events, answers to 'who/what') takes 이/가, not 은/는.

grammarNotes.title: 은/는 — topic continuity (an already-known topic)
grammarNotes.func: The topic marker 은/는 sets up what the sentence is ABOUT. Use it for something already known, already mentioned, or generally assumed — the shared starting point. It says 'as for X…' and then comments on it. It carries old information, not new.

formTable.when: topic noun ends in a consonant
topic noun ends in a vowel

examples.en: I'm a student.
examples.note: 'I' is the obvious shared topic of self-introduction, so 는 frames it and the comment follows.

examples.en: That movie was really fun.
examples.note: 그 영화 is already known (we both know which movie), so 는 continues it as the topic.

examples.en: As for Korean, the pronunciation is hard.
examples.note: 한국어 is the established topic; the new comment is about its 발음 (which itself takes 이).

examples.en: The weather is nice today.
examples.note: 오늘 is the assumed frame ('as for today'), so 는 sets the scene and 날씨가 carries the new subject.

keyPoint.label: 은/는 = old, 이/가 = new
keyPoint.body: First mention introduces with 이/가; once it's on the table, you keep talking about it with 은/는. 옛날에 한 남자가 살았어요. 그 남자는… (A man lived… The man…).

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 은 after a consonant resyllabifies: 선생님은 → 선생니믄; 책은 → 채근. Keep 는 as a clear 'neun' with no vowel reduction.

drill.instruction: Add 은 or 는 to set the already-known topic.
items: 그 책___ 재미있어요. (그 책 = the book we mentioned) → 그 책은

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: For self-introduction the speaker is the assumed topic, so use 저는, not 저가. Also note 저 + 가 irregularly becomes 제가 when you DO need focus ('I' as the one who did it) — 저가 is never correct.

grammarNotes.title: 은/는 — contrast and limited scope
grammarNotes.func: Beyond topic-setting, 은/는 marks CONTRAST: 'X (but as for something else, it's different).' It quietly implies a comparison, even when the other side is unspoken. Use it to set one item against another, or to limit a statement to just that item.

formTable.ex: 고기는 안 먹어요. (meat, at least, I don't eat)
이건 알아요. (this one I do know — others maybe not)

examples.en: My older brother is tall. I'm short.
examples.note: Two 는 set the siblings in direct contrast — tall vs. short.

examples.en: I like coffee but not tea.
examples.note: 는 on both objects (not 를) signals the explicit coffee-vs-tea contrast.

examples.en: Korean, at least, I can speak.
examples.note: 는 here limits the claim to Korean, implying 'other languages, maybe not.'

examples.en: Today I'm not busy (other days, I am).
examples.note: 는 on 오늘 contrasts today against the implied busy other days.

keyPoint.label: 는 over 가/를 = contrast is intended
keyPoint.body: 커피를 마셔요 = plain 'I drink coffee.' 커피는 마셔요 = 'Coffee I drink (but something else, no).' Swapping 를→는 (or 가→는) adds an unspoken 'unlike the rest.'

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In the contrast reading, 는/은 often carries a slight emphatic stress: 저'는 작아요. That extra stress is what flags the contrast aloud.

drill.instruction: Replace the neutral marker with 은/는 to add a contrast nuance.
drill.model: 고기를 안 먹어요. (contrast) → 고기는 안 먹어요.
items: 주말에 일해요. (but weekdays, no) → 주말___ 일해요. → 주말은
동생은 와요. (but I'm not coming) → 저___ 안 가요. → 저는

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English shows contrast with 'but' and word order, so learners keep 을/를 on both objects. Korean signals the contrast on the noun itself by switching 을/를 to 는 — leaving 를 there flattens the intended comparison.

grammarNotes.title: 이/가 — 'this exact one' (exclusive identification)
grammarNotes.func: When you single out ONE item as the answer — 'it is THIS one, not the others' — the identified subject takes 이/가. This exclusive-focus use is why 이/가 (not 은/는) appears in answers, in 'who/what' replies, and in 'it's X that…' sentences. It pins down the exact one.

formTable.ex: 이 책이 제일 좋아요. (THIS book is the best.)
이게 제 거예요. (THIS one is mine.)

examples.en: THIS person is my teacher.
examples.note: 이 사람 is singled out from others present, so 이 marks the exclusive identification.

examples.en: Who did it? — I did.
examples.note: Answering 'who' pins down the exact doer; 저+가 → 제가 carries that exclusive focus.

examples.en: Which bag do you like?
examples.note: 어느 (which) forces a one-out-of-many choice, so the subject takes 이.

examples.en: THIS is exactly the right answer.
examples.note: 바로 + 이게 (이것이) drives home 'this exact one and no other' — classic 이/가 focus.

keyPoint.label: 이/가 identifies, 은/는 describes
keyPoint.body: 이 사람이 김 선생님이에요 = 'THIS (one) is Mr. Kim' (picks him out). 이 사람은 김 선생님이에요 = 'As for this person, he's Mr. Kim' (just tells you about him). Use 이/가 to single out the exact one.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 이것이 commonly contracts to 이게, 그것이 → 그게, 저것이 → 저게 in speech. Learn the contracted 이게/그게/저게 as the everyday spoken forms.

drill.instruction: Fill in 이 or 가 to single out the exact one being identified.
items: 어느 게 더 싸요? → 이것___ 더 싸요. → 이것이 (이게)
이 가방___ 제일 예뻐요. → 이 가방이

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Answering a 'who' question identifies the exact doer, which demands 이/가, but English speakers reach for the topic-like 저는. 저는 했어요 sounds like 'As for me, I did (but talk about others separately)' — not a clean answer to 'who.'

grammarNotes.title: N은/는 N이/가 … — topic + inner subject in one sentence
grammarNotes.func: Korean often uses BOTH markers in a single sentence: 은/는 names the big-picture topic, then 이/가 names the specific thing the comment is really about. Pattern: '[Topic]은/는 [inner subject]이/가 [adjective/verb].' This is the natural way to describe a part, trait, or condition of something — 'As for the elephant, its nose is long.'

formTable.ex: 코끼리는 코가 길어요. (The elephant's nose is long.)
저는 강아지가 좋아요. (As for me, I like dogs.)
한국어는 발음이 어려워요. (Korean — its pronunciation is hard.)

examples.en: An elephant's nose is long.
examples.note: 코끼리 is the topic (은/는); 코 is the inner subject (이/가) that 길어요 actually describes.

examples.en: I don't have time.
examples.note: Literally 'As for me, time doesn't exist.' 저 = topic (는), 시간 = subject of 없다 (이).

examples.en: My older brother is tall.
examples.note: 형 is the topic; 키 (height) is the inner subject of 크다. You can't say 형은 커요 for 'tall.'

examples.en: This restaurant's kimchi stew is delicious.
examples.note: 식당 = topic (은); 김치찌개 = inner subject (가). The comment is really about the dish.

keyPoint.label: One topic (은/는), one inner subject (이/가)
keyPoint.body: Don't pile two 은/는 or two 이/가. The big thing you're talking about takes 은/는; the specific thing the predicate describes takes 이/가. 저는 머리가 아파요 = 'I have a headache' (me = topic, head = what hurts).

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 코가 = ko-ga (smooth, no stop); 키가 = ki-ga; 시간이 = sigani (final ㄴ links onto 이). Keep both syllables of 이/가 light — the stress sits on the predicate (길어요, 커요).

drill.instruction: Build the sentence with 은/는 on the topic and 이/가 on the inner subject.
drill.model: 나 / 머리 / 아프다 → 저는 머리가 아파요.
items: 기린 / 목 / 길다 → 기린은 목이 길어요.
저 / 동생 / 있다 → 저는 동생이 있어요.
이 커피 / 맛 / 좋다 → 이 커피는 맛이 좋아요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 코끼리가 코가 길어요. / 저는 시간은 없어요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 코끼리는 코가 길어요. / 저는 시간이 없어요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English has one subject per clause, so learners either mark the whole thing with 이/가 (코끼리가 코가...) or repeat 은/는. Korean splits the roles: the overall topic gets 은/는, and the specific noun the predicate is about gets 이/가 — exactly one of each.

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 전화했어요. 그 친구는 자주 전화하지 않아요.
exampleSentence.en: A friend called. That friend does not call often.
exampleSentence.note: First mention uses 가; continued topic uses 는.

exampleSentence.ko: 메시지는 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I send messages, but I do not call much.
exampleSentence.note: 전화는 contrasts calls with messages.

exampleSentence.ko: 누가 먼저 연락했어요? 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
exampleSentence.en: Who contacted first? I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 제가 answers 누가 with focus.

exampleSentence.ko: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I send messages often, but I do not call much.
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 makes the contrast visible.

exampleSentence.en: A text came, but no phone call came.
exampleSentence.note: 문자는 and 전화는 contrast two channels.

exampleSentence.en: Who contacted first?
exampleSentence.note: 누구 + 가 contracts to 누가.

exampleSentence.en: Today, I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 오늘은 contrasts today; 제가 identifies the actor.

exampleSentence.en: Does that friend call often?
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 keeps the friend as the topic while asking about habit.

exampleSentence.en: Usually they send messages, but today they called.
exampleSentence.note: 평소에는 contrasts the usual pattern with today.

exampleSentence.en: Today, I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 오늘은 contrasts today with other days.

exampleSentence.ko: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I send messages often, but I do not call much.
exampleSentence.note: The object 메시지 takes 를; the contrast uses 는.

exampleSentence.en: The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
exampleSentence.note: 질문은 is the contrastive topic.

exampleSentence.en: The answer was difficult.
exampleSentence.note: 대답이 introduces the part that was difficult.

exampleSentence.en: As for my opinion, the thinking is a little different.
exampleSentence.note: 의견은 frames the topic; 생각이 states what differs.

exampleSentence.en: That idea is good, but the reason is lacking.
exampleSentence.note: 생각은 frames the idea; 이유가 introduces the problem.

exampleSentence.en: For this issue, the reason is the most important thing.
exampleSentence.note: 문제는 sets the frame; 이유가 is the key subject.

exampleSentence.en: What is important? The reason is important.
exampleSentence.note: 이유가 answers 무엇이.

exampleSentence.en: The two expressions have a difference.
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 frames the two expressions; 차이가 states what exists.

exampleSentence.ko: 이런 상황에서는 제가 먼저 말해야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: In this kind of situation, I should speak first.
exampleSentence.note: 상황에서는 frames the condition; 제가 identifies the actor.

exampleSentence.en: The truth is, I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 사실은 frames the correction.

exampleSentence.en: As for the two people, their opinions are different.
exampleSentence.note: 두 사람은 is the frame; 의견이 is the differing subject.

exampleSentence.en: The meaning is the same, but the feeling is different.
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 contrasts meaning and feeling.

exampleSentence.en: The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
exampleSentence.note: 쉬웠는데 sets up contrast.

exampleSentence.en: For this issue, the reason is most important.
exampleSentence.note: 중요하다 often appears with the focused subject marked by 이/가.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two friends analyze a call and a message while the particles track new information, topic, contrast, and focus.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: A friend called yesterday.
lines.grammarNote: 친구가 introduces the caller as new information.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Does that friend call often?
lines.grammarNote: The friend is now the topic, so 그 친구는 is natural.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 아니요. 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
lines.romanization: aniyo. pyeongsoeneun mesijireul bonaeneunde oneureun jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
lines.en: No. Usually they send messages, but today I contacted them first.
lines.grammarNote: 평소에는 and 오늘은 contrast time frames; 제가 focuses the actor.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Who contacted first?
lines.grammarNote: 누가 asks for the focused subject.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 제가 먼저 연락했어요. 질문은 쉬웠는데 대답이 어려웠어요.
lines.romanization: jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo. jilmuneun swiwonneunde daedabi eoryeowosseoyo.
lines.en: I contacted first. The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
lines.grammarNote: 제가 answers who; 질문은 contrasts with 대답이.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그럼 이 문제는 이유가 제일 중요하네요.
lines.romanization: geureom i munjeneun iyuga jeil jungyohaneyo.
lines.en: Then for this issue, the reason is the most important thing.
lines.grammarNote: 이 문제는 frames the topic; 이유가 is the important subject.

readingText.title: 친구가에서 그 친구는으로
readingText.body: 어제 민서에게 친구가 전화했다. 처음 말할 때는 누가 전화했는지가 새 정보였기 때문에 친구가 자연스러웠다. 그다음 지훈은 "그 친구는 자주 전화해?"라고 물었다. 이미 말한 친구를 다시 주제로 삼았기 때문에 그 친구는이 맞았다. 민서는 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했다고 설명했다. 여기서 평소에는과 오늘은은 서로 대비된다. 지훈이 "누가 먼저 연락했어?"라고 묻자 민서는 "제가 먼저 연락했어"라고 답했다. 제가는 다른 사람이 아니라 바로 민서가 했다는 뜻이다. 마지막으로 "이 문제는 이유가 중요해"처럼 말하면, 문제는 이야기의 틀이고 이유가 그 안에서 중요한 새 정보가 된다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Yesterday, a friend called Minseo. On the first mention, who called was new information, so 친구가 was natural. Then Jihoon asked, "Does that friend call often?" Because the friend had already been mentioned and was now the topic, 그 친구는 was right. Minseo explained that usually the friend sends messages, but today she contacted first. Here 평소에는 and 오늘은 contrast with each other. When Jihoon asked, "Who contacted first?" Minseo answered, "I contacted first." 제가 means it was specifically Minseo, not someone else. Finally, in a sentence like "For this issue, the reason is important," 문제는 is the frame of the discussion and 이유가 is the important new information inside it.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 처음에는 왜 친구가를 썼어요?
평소에는과 오늘은은 어떤 역할을 해요?
이 문제는 이유가 중요해요에서 문제와 이유의 역할은 무엇이에요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 문제는 이야기의 틀이고, 이유가 그 안에서 중요한 새 정보예요.

culturalNote.title: 조사는 대화의 카메라다
culturalNote.body: Korean particles move the camera of the conversation. 이/가 zooms in on the subject that matters now. 은/는 sets the frame or contrasts one frame with another. This is why native speakers can hear a difference between 제가 했어요 and 저는 했어요 even when both contain I. 제가 answers who did it. 저는 often sounds like as for me, possibly contrasting with someone else.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing a particle, ask whether the noun is the new answer, the continuing topic, or one side of a contrast.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence introduces the caller as new information?
inlineExercises.explanation: 친구가 answers who called.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence contrasts messages and calls?
options: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
메시지가 자주 보내지만 전화가 잘 안 해요.
메시지에게 자주 보내지만 전화에게 안 해요.
inlineExercises.correct: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 은/는 marks the two contrasted communication methods.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which answer fits 누가 먼저 연락했어요?
inlineExercises.explanation: 제가 gives the focused who-answer.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which particles complete the topic-plus-subject sentence: 이 문제____ 이유____ 중요해요?
inlineExercises.explanation: 이 문제는 sets the frame; 이유가 is the important subject inside it.

inlineExercises.prompt: 이 문제___ 이유___ 중요해요. (As for this problem, the reason is important.)
inlineExercises.explanation: The outer topic is 이 문제는, and the inner subject is 이유가. This topic-plus-subject structure is common in Korean.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'My friend called first.'
inlineExercises.explanation: When answering 누가 first acted, the focused subject takes 가. 먼저 tells who acted first.

inlineExercises.prompt: Contrast messages and calls: 'I often send texts. I do not call much.'
inlineExercises.correct: 문자는 자주 보내요. 전화는 잘 안 해요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 은/는 marks contrast between texts and calls. The topic stays clear across the two sentences.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the focused answer to 누가 왔어요?: '친구는 왔어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: A focused answer to 누가 uses 이/가. 친구는 would sound like contrast or topic continuation.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence introduces the caller as new information?
inlineExercises.explanation: New or focused subject information uses 이/가. 은/는 would frame or contrast the friend.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'A message came.'
inlineExercises.explanation: The new thing that arrived takes 가. 메시지는 would sound like you are contrasting messages with something else.

bullets: 이/가 introduces or focuses the subject: 친구가 전화했어요, 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
은/는 continues or frames the topic: 그 친구는 자주 전화해요?, 이 문제는...
은/는 also marks contrast: 평소에는..., 오늘은..., 메시지는..., 전화는...
A Korean sentence can have both: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.

writingTask.prompt: Answer a friend who asks 'Who texted you first today?' Reply naming who it was, then add what you usually do — choosing 은/는 vs 이/가 by what's new vs known.
writingTask.hint: Use 이/가 to identify the new/focused subject (친구가 보냈어요), and 은/는 for the known topic or contrast (저는 …, 평소에는 …).
writingTask.model: 오늘은 친구가 먼저 문자를 보냈어요. 저는 평소에 먼저 연락을 안 해요. 그 친구는 자주 메시지를 보내요.
writingTask.modelEn: Today my friend texted first. I usually don't reach out first. That friend often sends messages.

canDo: Spotlight a new or focused subject with 이/가 (친구가 보냈어요)
Set up an already-known topic with 은/는 (저는 …, 그 친구는 …)
Mark contrast or limited scope with 은/는 (평소에는 …)
Combine topic and inner subject in one sentence (N은/는 N이/가 …)

chapters.title: Advanced Written Korean
chapters.goal: Make formal writing easier to follow with clear connectors.
chapters.scenario: You write a short report, complaint, summary, or project update.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: This report lacks evidence.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
dialogue.romanization: geureona haeksim jujangeun yujihal su itseumnida.
dialogue.en: However, the main claim can be maintained.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: By contrast, the case analysis needs strengthening.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 한편 예상되는 반론도 따로 검토해야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: hanpyeon yesangdoeneun ballondo ttaro geomtohaeya hamnida.
dialogue.en: Meanwhile, the expected counterarguments must also be reviewed separately.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 즉, 결론보다 근거와 논리를 보완해야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: jeuk, gyeollonboda geungeowa nollireul bowanhaeya hamnida.
dialogue.en: In other words, the evidence and reasoning need more work than the conclusion.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 결국 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: gyeolguk bogoseoneun jujang, geungeo, saryega seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya hamnida.
dialogue.en: Ultimately, a report's claim, evidence, and cases must be connected.

chapters.guidedPractice: Revise a weak report paragraph: add one sentence with 따라서, one contrast with 그러나 or 반면에, one clarification with 즉, and one final synthesis with 결국.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write four formal sentences using two connectors such as 따라서, 그러나, 즉, or 결국.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a claim and two pieces of evidence; decide whether the conclusion, evidence, logic, or counterargument needs revision.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 따라서, 그러나, 반면에, 한편, 즉, and 결국 cannot be swapped freely in a formal paragraph?

beginnerGuide.title: Register first
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter is about written reasoning, not casual conversation. A paragraph with 따라서 or 그러나 should usually keep formal endings such as -다, -한다, -이다, or formal polite -습니다.

beginnerGuide.title: Connector roles
beginnerGuide.body: Use 따라서 for a conclusion from evidence, 그러나 for direct contrast, 반면에 for two-sided comparison, 한편 for a parallel development, 즉 for restatement, and 결국 for final synthesis.

beginnerGuide.title: Argument vocabulary
beginnerGuide.body: Read 근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, and 반론 as one set. These words let you diagnose what is weak in a report instead of only saying the Korean is difficult.

checkpoints: I can choose a connector that matches the relationship between sentences.
I can keep formal connectors and formal endings in the same register.
I can revise a paragraph so the reader can follow the claim and reason.

curriculumTrack.label: C1 Written & Synthesis
curriculumTrack.description: Formal writing, internet register awareness, and whole-course production checks.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Make formal writing easier to follow with clear connectors.
exitTask.prompt: Write four formal sentences using two connectors such as 따라서, 그러나, 즉, or 결국.

sampleAnswer.ko: 자료가 부족합니다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 합니다. 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
sampleAnswer.en: The data is insufficient. Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again. However, the main claim can be maintained.

checklist: I can choose a connector that matches the relationship between sentences.
I can keep formal connectors and formal endings in the same register.
I can revise a paragraph so the reader can follow the claim and reason.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: You are revising a report or short essay. The Korean must show how one sentence follows from another: evidence leads to a conclusion, a contrast limits the claim, and a final sentence synthesizes the argument.
objectives: Choose formal connectors according to sentence relationship, not English translation.
Use report vocabulary such as 근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, and 반론 as one argument set.
Keep written connectors and written-register endings consistent in the same paragraph.
hook.whyItMatters: A learner can know every word in a paragraph and still sound weak if the connectors do not match the logic. This chapter teaches the glue that makes formal Korean writing read like an argument instead of a list of sentences.

grammarNotes.title: 따라서 / 그러므로 — Therefore (evidence to conclusion)
grammarNotes.func: These are the written-register connectors for drawing a logical conclusion from what you just said. They mark the jump from a reason or premise to its result, the way English uses 'therefore.' In conversation Koreans say 그래서, but in essays, reports, and articles they switch to 따라서 or 그러므로. Both open a new sentence.

formTable.when: Evidence stated, you give the result (most neutral, the everyday choice in reports and essays)
formTable.ex: 근거가 부족하다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.

formTable.when: A more deductive 'thus, it follows that'; slightly weightier, common in arguments
formTable.ex: 누구나 실수를 한다. 그러므로 검토가 필요하다.

formTable.when: The casual spoken version you REPLACE in formal writing (shown for contrast)
formTable.ex: 비가 와서 안 갔어 → 비가 왔다. 따라서 가지 않았다.

examples.ko: 이 보고서는 근거가 부족하다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.
examples.romanization: i bogoseoneun geungeoga bujokhada. ttaraseo gyeolloneul dasi geomtohaeya handa.
examples.en: This report lacks evidence. Therefore the conclusion must be reviewed again.
examples.note: 따라서 opens the sentence and draws the result straight from the stated problem.

examples.ko: 자료의 출처가 분명하지 않다. 그러므로 핵심 근거로 쓰기 어렵다.
examples.romanization: jaryoui chulcheoga bunmyeonghaji anta. geureomeuro haeksim geungeoro sseugi eoryeopda.
examples.en: The source of the material is unclear. Thus it is hard to use as key evidence.
examples.note: 그러므로 signals a firm 'it follows that,' suiting an argument.

examples.ko: 조사 대상이 제한적이다. 따라서 결과를 일반화하기 어렵다.
examples.romanization: josa daesangi jehanjeogida. ttaraseo gyeolgwareul ilbanhwahagi eoryeopda.
examples.en: The sample is limited. Therefore the result is hard to generalize.
examples.note: The limitation comes first, then 따라서 introduces the warranted conclusion.

examples.ko: 수요가 계속 줄고 있다. 그러므로 생산을 늘릴 이유가 없다.
examples.romanization: suyoga gyesok julgo itda. geureomeuro saengsaneul nullil iyuga eopda.
examples.en: Demand keeps falling. Thus there is no reason to raise production.
examples.note: 그러므로 ties a firm conclusion to the trend just described.

keyPoint.label: 따라서 vs 그러므로
keyPoint.body: Both mean 'therefore' and both are formal. 따라서 is the everyday workhorse of reports and essays — neutral and safe. 그러므로 feels a notch more deductive ('it necessarily follows'), so it shines in arguments and reasoning. In ordinary expository writing, default to 따라서; reach for 그러므로 when you want the logic to feel airtight.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 따라서 starts with a tense ㄸ: [tta-ra-seo]. 그러므로 is four light, even syllables [geu-reo-meu-ro] with no tense consonants — don't stress it like English 'therefore.'

drill.instruction: Replace the casual 그래서 with a formal connector (따라서 or 그러므로) to fit an essay.
items: 모든 조건이 같다. ___ 결과도 같아야 한다.
참가자가 늘었다. ___ 더 큰 장소가 필요하다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English writers tend to splice 'therefore' on with a comma in the middle of a sentence. In formal Korean, 따라서/그러므로 normally start a NEW sentence after a full stop. Hooking it onto the previous clause with a comma reads as a run-on.

grammarNotes.title: 그러나 / 반면에 / 한편 — three kinds of contrast
grammarNotes.func: Formal writing splits into three the contrast that casual 하지만 lumps together. 그러나 directly reverses or limits what you just said ('however'). 반면에 sets two things side by side as opposites ('by contrast, whereas'). 한편 moves to a separate, co-occurring point ('meanwhile, for its part') without contradicting. Picking the right one is a mark of polished writing.

formTable.when: Direct reversal or limitation of the previous claim — the strong written 'however'
formTable.ex: 핵심 주장은 분명하다. 그러나 근거가 부족하다.

formTable.when: Comparing two items as contrasting opposites; often after stating side A
formTable.ex: 첫 사례는 적절하다. 반면에 두 번째 사례는 약하다.

formTable.when: Adding a separate, co-occurring angle or new actor — not a contradiction
formTable.ex: 보고서는 비용을 강조한다. 한편 안전 검토는 부족하다.

examples.ko: 핵심 주장은 분명하다. 그러나 이를 뒷받침할 근거가 부족하다.
examples.romanization: haeksim jujangeun bunmyeonghada. geureona ireul dwitbatchimhal geungeoga bujokhada.
examples.en: The main claim is clear. However, the evidence to support it is insufficient.
examples.note: 그러나 directly limits the positive first sentence.

examples.ko: 첫 번째 사례는 적절하다. 반면에 두 번째 사례는 관련성이 약하다.
examples.romanization: cheot beonjjae saryeneun jeokjeolhada. banmyeone du beonjjae saryeneun gwallyeonseongi yakada.
examples.en: The first case is fitting. By contrast, the second case is weakly relevant.
examples.note: 반면에 lines up two comparable cases as opposites.

examples.ko: 보고서는 비용 문제를 강조한다. 한편 안전 문제 검토는 충분하지 않다.
examples.romanization: bogoseoneun biyong munjereul gangjohanda. hanpyeon anjeon munje geomtoneun chungbunhaji anta.
examples.en: The report stresses the cost issue. Meanwhile, the review of safety is not sufficient.
examples.note: 한편 shifts to a separate line of discussion, not a flat contradiction.

examples.ko: 이론은 단순하다. 그러나 적용은 결코 쉽지 않다.
examples.romanization: ironeun dansunhada. geureona jeogyongeun gyeolko swipji anta.
examples.en: The theory is simple. However, applying it is by no means easy.
examples.note: 그러나 flags a sharp 'but in reality' reversal, stronger than 하지만.

keyPoint.label: 그러나 vs 반면에 vs 한편
keyPoint.body: Test by relationship: if B cancels or limits A, use 그러나 (however). If B is the mirror-opposite of A, weighed against it, use 반면에 (by contrast). If B is just a separate development from another side, use 한편 (meanwhile). A common error is using 한편 where 반면에 is needed — 한편 does NOT mean 'in contrast,' it means 'from another quarter, at the same time.'

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 반면에 is [ban-myeo-ne] — the ㄴ of 면 links into 에, so it flows as one word, not 반/면/에 chopped apart. 한편 is [han-pyeon].

drill.instruction: Choose 그러나, 반면에, or 한편 for the contrast type shown in brackets.
drill.model: 가격은 올랐다. ___ 판매량은 그대로다. [two opposites compared] → 반면에
items: 모두 찬성할 줄 알았다. ___ 반대가 거셌다. [direct reversal]
서울은 비가 왔다. ___ 부산은 맑았다. [two opposites compared]
연구진은 실험을 이어갔다. ___ 학계는 논쟁을 벌였다. [separate co-occurring angle]

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 한편, 이 방법은 비싸다. (intending 'however, this method is expensive')
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners map 한편 to 'however' because dictionaries gloss it as 'on the other hand.' But 한편 means 'meanwhile, from another side,' not rebuttal. To overturn a claim use 그러나; to weigh two opposites use 반면에. Using 한편 for a flat contradiction confuses Korean readers.

grammarNotes.title: 즉 / 다시 말해서 — that is, in other words (restate, don't add)
grammarNotes.func: These connectors signal that what follows is a RESTATEMENT or clarification of what you just said — not new information. 즉 is a compact written 'namely, that is,' used to pin down a precise equivalent or definition. 다시 말해서 ('to put it again, in other words') reframes the whole idea in plainer words. Both tell the reader: same point, said more clearly.

formTable.when: Pinpointing an exact equivalent or narrower meaning — terse, very written 'namely, that is'
formTable.ex: 핵심 변수, 즉 가격이 결과를 좌우한다.

formTable.when: Rephrasing the whole idea in plainer words for the reader
formTable.ex: 수요가 공급을 넘었다. 다시 말해서, 물건이 부족하다.

formTable.when: Shorter written variant of 다시 말해서, often before a clause
formTable.ex: 비용이 효용을 넘는다. 다시 말해 손해다.

examples.ko: 문제는 결론 자체가 아니다. 즉, 근거와 논리의 연결이 약하다는 점이다.
examples.romanization: munjeneun gyeollon jachega anida. jeuk, geungeowa nolliui yeongyeori yakadaneun jeomida.
examples.en: The problem is not the conclusion itself. That is, the link between evidence and reasoning is weak.
examples.note: 즉 restates the diagnosis in a more precise form, adding no new fact.

examples.ko: 이 문장은 너무 추상적이다. 다시 말해서, 독자가 떠올릴 사례가 없다.
examples.romanization: i munjangeun neomu chusangjeogida. dasi malhaeseo, dokjaga tteoolril saryega eopda.
examples.en: This sentence is too abstract. In other words, there is no example the reader can picture.
examples.note: 다시 말해서 reframes the abstract point in concrete, plainer terms.

examples.ko: 가장 중요한 요소, 즉 신뢰가 무너졌다.
examples.romanization: gajang jungyohan yoso, jeuk silloega muneojyeotda.
examples.en: The most important element — namely, trust — collapsed.
examples.note: 즉 equates the abstract 'most important element' with the concrete word 신뢰; it sits inside the sentence.

examples.ko: 지출이 수입을 넘었다. 다시 말해, 적자가 났다.
examples.romanization: jichuri suibeul neomeotda. dasi malhae, jeokjaga natda.
examples.en: Spending exceeded income. In other words, there was a deficit.
examples.note: 다시 말해 (the shorter form) restates the situation with its plain name.

keyPoint.label: 즉 vs 다시 말해서
keyPoint.body: 즉 is for a tight, near-mathematical equivalence ('X, namely Y') and often sits INSIDE a sentence right after the term it defines. 다시 말해서 is for rephrasing a whole idea more accessibly and usually starts a fresh sentence. Rule of thumb: 즉 swaps in a precise synonym; 다시 말해서 explains the same point again in different words. Neither one introduces new evidence — for that, use 또한 or 예를 들어.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 즉 is one tight syllable [jeuk], ending in a hard ㄱ stop. 다시 말해서 is [da-si mal-hae-seo], even and unstressed.

drill.instruction: Insert 즉 or 다시 말해서 so the second sentence restates (not adds to) the first.
drill.model: 이 글은 사례가 없다. ___ 추상적이다. → 다시 말해서
items: 문제는 결론이 아니다. ___ 근거가 약하다는 점이다.
매출은 늘었지만 이익은 줄었다. ___ 효율이 떨어졌다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 근거가 약하다. 즉, 새로운 사례를 하나 더 들 수 있다.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 근거가 약하다. 즉, 주장을 뒷받침하기 어렵다.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners use 즉 like a loose English 'so' and then add a brand-new point. But 즉 only RESTATES what was already said in a clearer form. If you are adding new evidence, use 또한 or 예를 들어; if a result follows, use 따라서.

grammarNotes.title: 결국 / 궁극적으로 — final synthesis (what it all comes to)
grammarNotes.func: These pull a chain of reasoning together and name the final point. 결국 means 'in the end, ultimately' — the result or conclusion reached after a process. 궁극적으로 is 'ultimately, fundamentally,' a touch more abstract and principle-like. They are not just 'finally' (which only marks the last item in time); they answer what everything has been leading to.

formTable.when: Summing up the result after a process or chain of points
formTable.ex: 여러 자료를 검토했지만 결국 같은 결론에 도달했다.

formTable.when: Stating the deepest, most general principle behind it all
formTable.ex: 궁극적으로 좋은 글은 주장과 근거가 연결되어야 한다.

formTable.when: Marking an awaited event that finally happens (NOT synthesis — contrast only)
formTable.ex: 드디어 보고서를 제출했다. (at last — not a conclusion)

examples.ko: 결국 이 보고서의 핵심은 결론을 바꾸는 것이 아니라 근거를 보완하는 것이다.
examples.romanization: gyeolguk i bogoseoui haeksimeun gyeolloneul bakkuneun geosi anira geungeoreul bowanhaneun geosida.
examples.en: Ultimately, the key point of this report is not to change the conclusion but to strengthen the evidence.
examples.note: 결국 gathers the whole discussion and names the real takeaway.

examples.ko: 궁극적으로 좋은 글은 주장, 근거, 반론이 서로 연결되어야 한다.
examples.romanization: gunggeukjeogeuro joeun geureun jujang, geungeo, balloni seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya handa.
examples.en: Ultimately, good writing requires the claim, evidence, and counterargument to connect.
examples.note: 궁극적으로 sounds broader and more principle-like than 결국.

examples.ko: 여러 자료를 검토했지만 결국 같은 결론에 도달했다.
examples.romanization: yeoreo jaryoreul geomtohaetjiman gyeolguk gateun gyeollone dochakhaetda.
examples.en: Several sources were reviewed, but in the end they reached the same conclusion.
examples.note: 결국 marks the final result after the process of reviewing.

examples.ko: 논의는 길었다. 그러나 결국 핵심은 하나였다.
examples.romanization: nonuineun gireotda. geureona gyeolguk haeksimeun hanayeotda.
examples.en: The discussion was long. However, in the end the key point was just one.
examples.note: 결국 closes a long buildup by naming the single point it all reduces to.

keyPoint.label: 결국 vs 궁극적으로 vs 드디어
keyPoint.body: 결국 names the result a process arrives at ('in the end'). 궁극적으로 names the deepest principle behind everything ('fundamentally, ultimately'), so it fits broad closing statements. Neither is 드디어, which only means an awaited event 'finally' happened — a time word, not a synthesis. Save 결국/궁극적으로 for a real summary; don't open every paragraph with them.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 결국 is [gyeol-guk], two syllables both ending in a hard stop. 궁극적으로 is [gung-geuk-jeo-geu-ro], five even syllables — keep it steady, don't rush the middle.

drill.instruction: Fill the blank with 결국 or 드디어 by meaning: synthesis-of-a-process vs awaited-event-at-last.
drill.model: 오래 기다린 끝에 ___ 결과가 나왔다. → 드디어
items: 여러 안을 비교했지만 ___ 첫 안으로 돌아왔다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 오래 준비한 발표를 결국 끝냈다. (intending 'I finally finished it!')
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'finally' covers both 'at long last' and 'in conclusion,' so learners reach for 결국 for an awaited relief. But 결국 carries a result-of-a-process nuance (often a slightly resigned 'in the end'). For the happy 'at last' sense, use 드디어.

grammarNotes.title: Written endings — -다 / -ㄴ다·-는다 / -이다
grammarNotes.func: Formal connectors need formal endings around them. If a paragraph uses 따라서 but then ends every sentence in -해요, the logic sounds written but the voice sounds conversational. In expository Korean (essays, reports, articles) you use the plain written style: adjectives and the copula in -다, action verbs in -ㄴ다/-는다, and noun statements in -이다. This is the register that pairs with the connectors in this chapter.

formTable.when: Adjective or descriptive verb (the plain dictionary -다 carries the written meaning)
Action verb in expository prose — vowel stem +-ㄴ다, consonant stem +-는다
formTable.ex: 필자는 비용 문제를 강조한다. / 자료를 충분히 다루지 않는다.

examples.ko: 이 글은 사례가 부족하다. 따라서 설득력이 약하다.
examples.romanization: i geureun saryega bujokhada. ttaraseo seoldeungnyeogi yakada.
examples.en: This piece lacks examples. Therefore it is not very persuasive.
examples.note: Both sentences keep the plain written -다 on adjectives.

examples.ko: 필자는 비용 문제를 강조한다. 그러나 안전 문제는 충분히 다루지 않는다.
examples.romanization: piljaneun biyong munjereul gangjohanda. geureona anjeon munjeneun chungbunhi daruji anneunda.
examples.en: The writer stresses cost. However, the safety issue is not treated sufficiently.
examples.note: Action verbs in formal writing take -ㄴ다/-는다, not -해요.

examples.en: The key point is not the amount of material but its relevance.
examples.note: Noun conclusions take -이다.

examples.ko: 결국 좋은 글은 근거와 사례가 연결되어야 한다.
examples.romanization: gyeolguk joeun geureun geungeowa saryega yeongyeoldoeeoya handa.
examples.en: Ultimately, good writing requires evidence and cases to connect.
examples.note: -아야 한다 keeps the obligation in plain written style, matching 결국.

keyPoint.label: One register per paragraph
keyPoint.body: Decide the register first, then keep it. Expository writing uses the plain written style: adjectives/copula in -다·-이다 and action verbs in -ㄴ다/-는다. -습니다 is also formal and fits presentations and polite reports — but pick one. Mixing -해요 with academic connectors like 따라서 and 즉 makes a single paragraph feel stylistically uneven, even when every word is correct.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: -ㄴ다/-는다 endings end on a clean -다 [da]; don't soften them toward the spoken -다아. -이다 is [i-da], the 이 fully voiced after a consonant.

drill.instruction: Rewrite each -해요 sentence in plain written style (adjective/noun → -다/-이다, action verb → -ㄴ다/-는다).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners default to the safe spoken -해요 even after a written connector like 따라서. In an essay or report this clashes: the connector says 'formal writing,' the ending says 'conversation.' Match the ending to the register — use -다/-ㄴ다/-는다/-이다 throughout the paragraph.

exampleSentence.en: Evidence that supports the claim must be presented.
exampleSentence.note: Use 근거 when a claim needs support, not merely a reason.

exampleSentence.en: If the evidence is weak, the conclusion also loses persuasiveness.
exampleSentence.note: 결론 is the endpoint of reasoning, not a story ending.

exampleSentence.ko: 이 글의 핵심은 비용 문제가 아니라 안전 문제이다.
exampleSentence.en: The key point of this piece is not cost but safety.
exampleSentence.note: 핵심 narrows attention to the central issue.

exampleSentence.en: The claim is clear, but there is a leap in the reasoning.
exampleSentence.note: Say 논리에 비약이 있다, not 논리가 비약하다.

exampleSentence.ko: 주장을 뒷받침하려면 구체적인 사례를 제시해야 한다.
exampleSentence.en: To support a claim, concrete cases must be presented.
exampleSentence.note: 사례 is more formal and analytical than 예.

exampleSentence.en: However, expected counterarguments must also be reviewed.
exampleSentence.note: A strong formal paragraph anticipates objections.

exampleSentence.ko: 자료의 출처가 분명하지 않다. 따라서 핵심 근거로 사용하기 어렵다.
exampleSentence.en: The source of the material is unclear. Therefore, it is difficult to use as key evidence.
exampleSentence.note: 따라서 connects evidence to a formal consequence.

exampleSentence.ko: 핵심 주장은 분명하다. 그러나 근거가 부족하다.
exampleSentence.en: The main claim is clear. However, the evidence is insufficient.
exampleSentence.note: 그러나 gives a direct formal contrast.

exampleSentence.ko: 첫 번째 사례는 적절하다. 반면에 두 번째 사례는 관련성이 약하다.
exampleSentence.en: The first case is appropriate. By contrast, the second case is weakly relevant.
exampleSentence.note: 반면에 compares two sides.

exampleSentence.ko: 문제는 결론 자체가 아니다. 즉, 근거와 논리의 연결이 약하다는 점이다.
exampleSentence.en: The problem is not the conclusion itself. In other words, the link between evidence and reasoning is weak.
exampleSentence.note: 즉 clarifies the same point in a narrower form.

exampleSentence.ko: 결국 좋은 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 한다.
exampleSentence.en: Ultimately, a good report requires its claim, evidence, and cases to be connected.
exampleSentence.note: 결국 summarizes what the whole discussion leads to.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two classmates are revising a Korean report draft before submission.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: This report lacks evidence.
lines.grammarNote: 근거가 부족하다 is the diagnosis.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again.
lines.grammarNote: 따라서 links the diagnosis to the required action.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
lines.romanization: geureona haeksim jujangeun yujihal su itseumnida.
lines.en: However, the main claim can be maintained.
lines.grammarNote: 그러나 limits the criticism so the whole argument is not rejected.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: By contrast, the case analysis needs strengthening.
lines.grammarNote: 반면에 compares one part of the report with another.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 한편 예상되는 반론도 따로 검토해야 합니다.
lines.romanization: hanpyeon yesangdoeneun ballondo ttaro geomtohaeya hamnida.
lines.en: Meanwhile, the expected counterarguments also need to be reviewed separately.
lines.grammarNote: 한편 opens a related but parallel issue.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 즉, 결론보다 근거와 논리를 보완해야 합니다.
lines.romanization: jeuk, gyeollonboda geungeowa nollireul bowanhaeya hamnida.
lines.en: In other words, the evidence and reasoning need more work than the conclusion.
lines.grammarNote: 즉 restates the revision target more clearly.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 결국 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 합니다.
lines.romanization: gyeolguk bogoseoneun jujang, geungeo, saryega seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya hamnida.
lines.en: Ultimately, a report's claim, evidence, and cases must be connected.
lines.grammarNote: 결국 gives the final synthesis.

readingText.title: 근거가 부족한 보고서 고치기
readingText.body: 초안 보고서는 결론이 분명했으나 근거가 부족했다. 따라서 결론을 유지하되 사례 분석을 보완해야 한다. 그러나 모든 내용을 새로 쓸 필요는 없다. 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있다. 반면에 반론 검토는 아직 약하다. 즉, 문제는 결론 자체가 아니라 근거와 논리의 연결이다. 결국 좋은 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례, 반론이 서로 연결될 때 설득력을 가진다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: The draft report had a clear conclusion, but the evidence was insufficient. Therefore, the conclusion can remain, but the case analysis needs to be strengthened. However, not all content needs to be rewritten. The main claim can be kept. By contrast, the counterargument review is still weak. In other words, the problem is not the conclusion itself but the link between evidence and reasoning. Ultimately, a good report is persuasive when claim, evidence, cases, and counterarguments are connected.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 초안 보고서의 가장 큰 문제는 무엇인가요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 결론 자체가 아니라 근거와 논리의 연결이 약한 것입니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 왜 따라서가 쓰였나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 근거가 부족하다는 진단에서 사례 분석을 보완해야 한다는 결론이 이어지기 때문입니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 글의 마지막 문장에서 결국은 어떤 역할을 하나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 앞의 수정 방향을 모아 좋은 보고서의 조건으로 정리합니다.

culturalNote.title: Formal Korean writing is relationship logic
culturalNote.body: Korean essays and reports often sound polished because each connector tells the reader exactly how to process the next sentence. 그러나 does not merely mean 'but'; it tells the reader to revise the previous claim. 즉 does not merely mean 'so'; it tells the reader to reinterpret the same point more precisely.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing a connector, name the relationship in Korean: 결론, 대조, 비교, 보충, 재진술, or 종합.

inlineExercises.prompt: 근거가 부족하다. ___ 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: The second sentence is a consequence of the first.

inlineExercises.prompt: 첫 번째 사례는 적절하다. ___ 두 번째 사례는 관련성이 약하다.
inlineExercises.explanation: Two comparable sides are being contrasted.

inlineExercises.prompt: 문제는 결론이 아니다. ___ 근거와 논리의 연결이 약하다는 점이다.
inlineExercises.explanation: The second sentence restates the diagnosis more precisely.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps written register most consistently?
options: 결국 좋은 글은 근거와 사례가 연결되어야 한다.
결국 좋은 글은 근거랑 사례가 연결돼요.
결국 좋은 글은 근거랑 사례, 이런 게 중요해요.
inlineExercises.correct: 결국 좋은 글은 근거와 사례가 연결되어야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: 결국 plus -다 style keeps the paragraph formal and written.

inlineExercises.prompt: 근거___ 부족하다. (The evidence is insufficient.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 부족하다 describes the evidence, so 근거 takes 가. 를 would make evidence an object, which does not fit this adjective.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'The evidence is weak. Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed.'
inlineExercises.correct: 근거가 약하다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: 따라서 connects evidence to a conclusion or required action. The written ending -다 keeps the register consistent.

inlineExercises.prompt: Restate with “that is”: 문제는 결론이 아니다. ___ 근거와 논리의 연결이다.
inlineExercises.explanation: 즉 restates or clarifies the same point. It should not introduce an unrelated new contrast.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the written-register mismatch: '근거가 약하다 ㅋㅋ 따라서 다시 검토해야 한다.'
inlineExercises.correct: 근거가 약하다. 따라서 다시 검토해야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: ㅋㅋ belongs to casual chat, not a formal written paragraph. Removing it keeps the report register consistent.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which connector best contrasts two cases?
inlineExercises.explanation: 반면에 contrasts two sides or cases. 즉 restates, and 따라서 draws a conclusion.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'Ultimately, the core is logic.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 궁극적으로 gives final synthesis. -이다 keeps the written-register ending consistent.

bullets: 따라서: evidence or condition leads to a conclusion.
그러나: direct limitation or reversal. 반면에: two-sided comparison. 한편: related parallel development.
즉: restatement or clarification, not new evidence.
결국: final synthesis after a chain of reasoning.
근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, 반론 belong together in report and essay revision.

writingTask.prompt: Write a short expository paragraph (3-4 sentences) arguing a point, using formal written connectors and consistent written endings.
writingTask.hint: Use 따라서/그러므로 for the conclusion, 그러나/반면에 for contrast, 즉/다시 말해서 to restate, and written endings -다 / -ㄴ다·-는다 / -이다 throughout (not 해요).
writingTask.model: 운동은 건강에 중요하다. 그러나 시간이 없는 사람이 많다. 따라서 짧게라도 매일 걷는 것이 좋다. 즉, 운동은 길이보다 꾸준함이 핵심이다.
writingTask.modelEn: Exercise is important for health. However, many people have no time. Therefore, it is good to walk every day, even briefly. That is, for exercise, consistency rather than length is the key.

canDo: Draw a conclusion in formal writing with 따라서 / 그러므로 (따라서 …다)
Distinguish three kinds of contrast with 그러나 / 반면에 / 한편
Restate without adding new information using 즉 / 다시 말해서 (즉, …이다)
Keep a consistent written register with -다 / -ㄴ다·-는다 / -이다 endings (and 결국/궁극적으로 to synthesize)

chapters.title: Korean Internet Language and Colloquial Intensifiers
chapters.goal: Read casual Korean online without carrying it into formal writing.
chapters.scenario: You read comments, KakaoTalk messages, live chat, or social posts.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그 댓글 봤어? 완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ.
dialogue.romanization: geu daetgeul bwasseo? wanjeon utgyeo kkk.
dialogue.en: Did you see that comment? It's so funny lol.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yeah, I saw it. Whoa, did you hit like?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 응, 친구한테 공유했어. 댓글 반응도 레전드야.
dialogue.romanization: eung, chinguhante gongyuhaesseo. daetgeul baneungdo rejeondeuya.
dialogue.en: Yeah, I shared it with a friend. The comment reactions are legendary too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 공식 글에는 ㅋㅋ 빼고 재미있었습니다처럼 써야 해.
dialogue.romanization: gongsik geureneneun kk ppaego jaemiisseotseumnidacheoreom sseoya hae.
dialogue.en: In an official post, you should leave out ㅋㅋ and write something like 'it was interesting.'

chapters.guidedPractice: Rewrite five casual chat reactions for two settings: friend chat with ㅋㅋ/ㅇㅇ/완전, then official writing without slang.
chapters.realLifeTask: Sort three expressions into friend chat, polite chat, and formal writing.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner names a relationship: close friend, classmate, professor, company account, or livestream chat. Choose the reaction that fits the register.
chapters.review: Can you explain when ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, ㅇㅈ, 대박, 완전, 레전드, and 개웃겨 are natural and when to replace them?

beginnerGuide.title: Register first
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter is about relationship and channel. ㅋㅋ and ㅇㅇ can be perfect in a friend chat and still be rude or careless in an email, professor message, or company notice.

beginnerGuide.title: Reaction families
beginnerGuide.body: Read the forms as families: ㅋㅋ/ㅠㅠ for emotion, ㅇㅇ/ㅇㅈ/ㄹㅇ for agreement or truth, and 완전/진짜/대박/레전드/개웃겨 for intensity.

beginnerGuide.title: Platform actions
beginnerGuide.body: Match digital nouns with their natural verbs: 댓글을 달다, 좋아요를 누르다, 친구한테 공유하다, 라이브 채팅에 올라오다.

checkpoints: I can recognize ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, and ㅇㅈ.
I can use casual intensifiers like 완전, 진짜, 대박, and 레전드 with the right people.
I can remove internet markers from formal email or school writing.

curriculumTrack.label: B2 Advanced Control
curriculumTrack.description: Causatives, counterfactuals, nominalisation, attitude endings, discourse control, and register switching.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Read casual Korean online without carrying it into formal writing.
exitTask.prompt: Sort three expressions into friend chat, polite chat, and formal writing.

sampleAnswer.ko: 친구한테는 '완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋ'라고 해도 되지만, 공식 글에는 '재미있었습니다'라고 써야 해요.
sampleAnswer.en: To a friend, '완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋ' is okay, but in an official post, you should write 'it was interesting.'

checklist: I can recognize ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, and ㅇㅈ.
I can use casual intensifiers like 완전, 진짜, 대박, and 레전드 with the right people.
I can remove internet markers from formal email or school writing.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: You are reading a friend group chat, a comment thread, and a live chat. The Korean is short, fast, and emotional, but every reaction still has a social boundary.
objectives: Recognize Korean consonant reactions such as ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, and ㅇㅈ.
Use colloquial intensifiers such as 완전, 진짜, 대박, 레전드, and 개웃겨 only in suitable informal settings.
Rewrite casual chat reactions into safer polite or formal Korean when the relationship changes.
hook.whyItMatters: Internet Korean is not a separate toy language. It is register-sensitive Korean. A sentence that feels perfect in a group chat can sound rude to a professor or careless on a company account.

grammarNotes.title: Chat abbreviations: ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, ㅇㅈ
grammarNotes.func: These are consonant-only shorthand 'reaction' tokens Koreans type in chat (KakaoTalk, comments, DMs). They're not words you pronounce out loud; they're typed signals, almost like emoji. ㅋㅋ shows laughter, ㅠㅠ shows crying/sadness, and ㅇㅇ / ㄹㅇ / ㅇㅈ are clipped one-shot replies (yeah / for real / agreed). They make a message feel casual and friendly, which is exactly why you use them with friends and peers, never with a boss, teacher, or stranger.

formTable.when: Something is funny; softening a message; showing you're amused
formTable.ex: 아 진짜 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ (lol that's so funny)

formTable.when: Crying, sad, disappointed, or begging cutely
formTable.add: ㅠㅠ (also ㅜㅜ); pure emotion, no laugh
formTable.ex: 나 시험 망했어 ㅠㅠ (I bombed the test)

formTable.when: A short 'yeah / yes / ok' reply between friends
formTable.ex: ㅇㅇ 나도 갈게 (yeah, I'll go too)
ㄹㅇ 그 카페 맛있어 (that cafe's legit good)

formTable.when: Agreeing hard with what someone said
formTable.ex: ㅇㅈ 그 영화 별로였음 (agreed, that movie was meh)

examples.en: lololol you're so funny
examples.note: Repeating ㅋ = a bigger laugh; a single ㅋ can read as cold or sarcastic.

examples.en: It rained so the plan got cancelled
examples.note: ㅠㅠ carries the disappointment, so you don't need extra sad words.

examples.ko: A: 내일 시간 돼? / B: ㅇㅇ
examples.en: A: free tomorrow? / B: yep
examples.note: ㅇㅇ is a full reply on its own; typing 네 here would feel oddly stiff with a close friend.

examples.ko: ㄹㅇ ㅇㅈ 그 식당 줄 너무 길어
examples.romanization: ral injeong geu sikdang jul neomu gireo
examples.en: for real, agreed, that restaurant's line is way too long
examples.note: ㄹㅇ and ㅇㅈ often stack at the start of a message to pile on agreement.

keyPoint.label: Typed sound vs spoken word
keyPoint.body: ㅋㅋ and ㅠㅠ are typed, not spoken — you don't say 'kuh-kuh' out loud. ㅇㅇ / ㄹㅇ / ㅇㅈ are clipped spellings of 응응 / 레알 / 인정, so reading them aloud means saying the full word, not naming the letters.

drill.instruction: Pick the abbreviation that fits the reaction in brackets.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers treat 'haha/lol' as harmless filler, but dropping ㅋㅋ or ㅇㅇ into a message to a superior reads as flippant and too casual. Keep these for friends and peers only.

grammarNotes.title: Colloquial intensifiers: 완전 / 진짜 / 너무 / 대박 / 레전드
grammarNotes.func: These are casual booster words meaning roughly 'so / totally / really / insanely (good)'. Speakers drop them in front of an adjective or verb, or use them alone as an exclamation, to crank up the feeling. 진짜 and 너무 are everyday-neutral; 완전 sounds breezy and young; 대박 and 레전드 are slangy hype words for something amazing or unforgettable. They live in speech, chat, and reviews, and they carry the emotion that flat, polite sentences leave out.

formTable.when: 'so / totally' before an adjective; very common in casual talk
formTable.ex: 이거 완전 맛있어 (this is so good)

formTable.when: 'really / seriously'; the most neutral, works almost anywhere
'so (much)'; in casual speech often just means 'very', not 'excessively'
formTable.ex: 너무 좋아 (I love it / it's so nice)

formTable.when: 'awesome / no way!'; exclamation for shocking-good (or shocking-bad) news
'legendary / epic'; calling something unforgettably great (or hilariously bad)
formTable.ex: 어제 공연 레전드였어 (last night's show was legendary)

examples.en: This cafe's vibe is totally great
examples.note: 완전 sounds young and upbeat; in formal writing you'd use 아주/매우 instead.

examples.en: I'm seriously starving
examples.note: 진짜 is the safest intensifier — natural in chat and in spoken sentences alike.

examples.en: Whoa, no way — is that for real?
examples.note: 대박 works as a one-word reaction to surprising news, good or bad.

examples.ko: 어제 경기 봤어? 완전 레전드였어 ㅋㅋ
examples.en: Did you watch the game? It was an absolute legend lol
examples.note: 레전드 + 이다 turns the noun into 'was epic'; 완전 stacks on top for extra hype.

keyPoint.label: 너무: textbook 'too much' vs real-life 'very'
keyPoint.body: Textbooks teach 너무 = 'too (excessively)', but in everyday speech 너무 좋아 just means 'I love it', not 'I like it too much'. Context, not the word itself, decides whether it's negative.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 대박 is often stretched as 대애박~ for emphasis, and 헐 frequently leads into it (헐 대박). 완전 is written 완전 but in fast speech can sound like a quick 완젼.

drill.instruction: Fill each blank with a natural intensifier (more than one answer can work).
drill.model: 이 떡볶이 ___ 매워 → 이 떡볶이 진짜 매워

englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 그 영화 완전 대박이었어. / 그 영화 정말 좋았습니다.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Don't mix slang (대박, 완전) with formal endings (-습니다) or stiff adverbs (매우). Slang intensifiers belong with casual endings; when you need to sound polite or formal, switch to 정말/아주/매우 and drop the slang.

grammarNotes.title: Platform verbs: 댓글 달다, 좋아요 누르다, 공유하다, 구독하다
grammarNotes.func: Every social-media action in Korean has a fixed noun + verb pairing you have to memorize rather than translate from English. You 'hang' a comment (댓글을 달다), 'press' a like (좋아요를 누르다), 'share' (공유하다), and 'subscribe' (구독하다). The object particle 을/를 is often dropped in casual chat (댓글 달았어), but the verb pairing is fixed — pick the wrong verb and it sounds off even when every word is technically correct.

formTable.when: Leaving / writing a comment on a post or video
formTable.ex: 영상에 댓글 달았어 (I left a comment on the video)
사진에 좋아요 눌러 줘 (hit like on the photo)
이 글 친구한테 공유했어 (I shared this post with a friend)

formTable.when: Following a channel/creator to get new uploads
formTable.ex: 그 채널 구독했어 (I subscribed to that channel)

examples.en: Please subscribe and hit like!
examples.note: The set phrase every Korean YouTuber says; note 좋아요 pairs with 누르다, never 하다.

examples.en: Someone left a comment on my photo
examples.note: 달다 conjugates to 달았어 (darasseo); the 을 is dropped, which is normal in casual speech.

examples.ko: 이 영상 진짜 웃겨, 단톡방에 공유할게
examples.romanization: i yeongsang jinjja utgyeo, dantokbang-e gongyu-halge
examples.en: This video is hilarious, I'll share it to the group chat
examples.note: 공유하다 takes 에 for the destination (group chat) and 을/를 for the thing shared.

examples.en: It passed a thousand likes, awesome
examples.note: Here 좋아요 is the noun 'like(s)' being counted with 개, not the verb action.

keyPoint.label: 좋아요 누르다, not 좋아요 하다
keyPoint.body: English 'like' is one word, so learners reach for 좋아요 하다 — but Korean fixes each action to its own verb: a like is pressed (누르다), a comment is hung (달다). Memorize the pair instead of translating the verb.

drill.instruction: Complete each sentence with the right verb in the right form.
drill.model: 그 채널 좋아서 ___ → 그 채널 좋아서 구독했어
items: 내 글이 웃겼나 봐, 사람들이 댓글 많이 ___

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Two traps: (1) 좋아요 takes 누르다, not 하다; (2) for posting a comment Koreans say 댓글을 달다, not the literal 댓글을 쓰다. 쓰다 is fine for 'writing' the text itself, but 달다 is the platform action of posting it.

grammarNotes.title: Register: ㅇㅇ vs 네 / 알겠어요
grammarNotes.func: The same meaning ('yes / got it / agreed') wears very different clothes depending on who you're talking to. ㅇㅇ, 응, ㅇㅈ, and 반말 belong to text chat with close friends and peers. 네 / 알겠어요 / 알겠습니다 are what you say or type to anyone you respect — a teacher, a customer, an older person, a boss. Picking the wrong register isn't a grammar mistake; it's a social one. So before you reply, read the relationship: is this someone you'd speak 반말 to, or someone you owe 존댓말?

formTable.when: Close friend / peer, in chat — quick 'yeah'
formTable.ex: ㅇㅇ 거기서 보자 (yeah, see you there)
ㅇㅈ 그건 좀 너무했어 (agreed, that was a bit much)

examples.ko: A: 내일 회의 2시야 / B: ㅇㅇ 알았어
examples.en: A: tomorrow's meeting is at 2 / B: yep, got it
examples.note: Friend-to-friend, so ㅇㅇ + 반말 (알았어) is natural and warm.

examples.en: Yes, understood. I'll take care of it right away
examples.note: To a boss or client; 네 + 알겠습니다 is the safe default at work.

examples.en: Yes, I understand, teacher
examples.note: Even with a teacher you're close to, keep 네/알겠어요 — never ㅇㅇ.

examples.en: Mom texted back 'ㅇㅇ' so I laughed a little
examples.note: Shows ㅇㅇ as the casual marker — funny precisely because you don't expect it from a parent.

keyPoint.label: Register is a relationship choice, not a vocab choice
keyPoint.body: ㅇㅇ and 네 mean the same thing; what differs is who you're allowed to say it to. When unsure, default to 네/알겠어요 — being slightly too polite is invisible, but being too casual is rude.

drill.instruction: Choose ㅇㅇ or 네/알겠어요 for each reply based on who's speaking.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners who finally feel comfortable with chat slang start sprinkling ㅇㅇ everywhere, including replies to a boss or teacher. ㅇㅇ is 반말-level casual; to a superior it reads as curt and disrespectful. Match the register to the person: 존댓말 gets 네, not ㅇㅇ.

exampleSentence.en: This comment is so funny lol.
exampleSentence.note: Casual digital laughter.

exampleSentence.en: They say the assignment is due tomorrow T_T.
exampleSentence.note: Sad, frustrated, or playfully distressed reaction.

exampleSentence.en: Yeah, got it.
exampleSentence.note: Quick casual yes to a close peer.

exampleSentence.en: This song is seriously good.
exampleSentence.note: Truth/intensity marker from 리얼.

exampleSentence.ko: A: 이 댓글이 제일 웃겨. / B: ㅇㅈ.
exampleSentence.en: A: This comment is the funniest. / B: Agreed.
exampleSentence.note: Endorses an opinion or take.

exampleSentence.en: That video is totally funny.
exampleSentence.note: Casual intensifier, not formal writing.

exampleSentence.en: Today's live chat was legendary.
exampleSentence.note: Can be praise or ironic reaction.

exampleSentence.en: This comment is hilarious lolol.
exampleSentence.note: Very casual and rougher than 진짜 웃겨.

exampleSentence.en: I left a comment on that post.
exampleSentence.note: 댓글을 달다 is the standard collocation.

exampleSentence.en: I just hit like.
exampleSentence.note: The button is pressed, so use 누르다.

exampleSentence.en: It was funny, so I shared it with a friend.
exampleSentence.note: The recipient takes 한테 or 에게.

exampleSentence.ko: 라이브 채팅이 너무 빨라서 댓글을 다 못 읽었어.
exampleSentence.en: The live chat was so fast that I couldn't read all the comments.
exampleSentence.note: A natural place for short reactions.

extendedDialogue.setting: Friends react to a comment thread, then rewrite the same reaction for a formal setting.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그 댓글 봤어? 완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ.
lines.romanization: geu daetgeul bwasseo? wanjeon utgyeo kkk.
lines.en: Did you see that comment? It's so funny lol.
lines.grammarNote: 완전 and ㅋㅋ fit close-friend chat.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Yeah, I saw it. Whoa, did you hit like?
lines.grammarNote: ㅇㅇ is casual agreement; 좋아요 takes 누르다.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 응, 친구한테 공유했어. 댓글 반응도 레전드야.
lines.romanization: eung, chinguhante gongyuhaesseo. daetgeul baneungdo rejeondeuya.
lines.en: Yeah, I shared it with a friend. The comment reactions are legendary too.
lines.grammarNote: 친구한테 marks who received the shared content.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 공식 글에는 ㅋㅋ 빼고 재미있었습니다처럼 써야 해.
lines.romanization: gongsik geureneneun kk ppaego jaemiisseotseumnidacheoreom sseoya hae.
lines.en: In an official post, you should leave out ㅋㅋ and write something like 'it was interesting.'
lines.grammarNote: The same reaction must be rewritten when the register changes.

readingText.title: 친구 단톡방과 공식 글 구분하기
readingText.body: 친구 단톡방에서는 이 댓글 완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ처럼 짧고 감정적인 표현이 자연스럽다. ㅇㅇ은 빠른 대답이고, ㄹㅇ ㅇㅈ은 상대의 의견에 강하게 동의하는 반응이다. 라이브 채팅에서는 이런 표현이 빠르게 올라오기 때문에 글이 문장보다 반응에 가깝다. 그러나 교수님께 보내는 메시지나 회사 계정의 공식 글에서는 같은 표현을 그대로 쓰면 가볍거나 무례하게 들릴 수 있다. 이때는 네, 확인했습니다, 정말 재미있었습니다, 저도 그렇게 생각합니다처럼 완전한 문장으로 바꾸는 것이 안전하다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: In a friend group chat, short emotional lines like 'this comment is so funny lol' feel natural. ㅇㅇ is a quick answer, and ㄹㅇ ㅇㅈ strongly agrees with someone's opinion. In live chat, these forms appear quickly, so the writing feels more like reactions than full sentences. However, if you use the same expressions in a message to a professor or an official company post, they can sound too casual or rude. In those settings, it is safer to rewrite them as full sentences such as 'Yes, I have confirmed it,' 'It was really interesting,' or 'I also think so.'

comprehensionQuestions.question: 친구 단톡방에서 자연스러운 표현은 무엇인가요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 이 댓글 완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ 같은 짧고 감정적인 표현입니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: ㄹㅇ ㅇㅈ은 어떤 반응인가요?
공식 글에서는 왜 표현을 바꿔야 하나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 그대로 쓰면 가볍거나 무례하게 들릴 수 있기 때문입니다.

culturalNote.title: Slang depends on the relationship, not only the platform
culturalNote.body: A KakaoTalk message is not automatically casual. A group chat with close friends allows ㅋㅋ, ㅇㅇ, and 개웃겨. A KakaoTalk message to a professor or workplace manager still needs 네, 확인했습니다, 감사합니다, and complete sentences. Korean digital language is fast, but hierarchy and relationship still matter.
culturalNote.tip: Before using slang, ask two questions: Are we close? Is this channel private and informal?

inlineExercises.prompt: A close friend asks, 내일 7시에 볼까? Which reply fits casual chat?
inlineExercises.explanation: ㅇㅇ is natural only with close peers.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is safest for a professor after a funny class video?
inlineExercises.explanation: The polite/formal sentence keeps the reaction respectful.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which verb naturally goes with 좋아요?
inlineExercises.explanation: 좋아요 is treated as a button, so Koreans press it.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which expression agrees with someone's opinion?
inlineExercises.explanation: ㅇㅈ comes from 인정 and means agreed or true that.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which expression is very casual and rougher than 진짜 웃겨?
inlineExercises.explanation: 개웃겨 is natural in close peer chat but too rough for formal settings.

inlineExercises.prompt: 댓글___ 달았어요. (I left a comment.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 댓글을 달다 is the natural verb phrase for leaving a comment. 이 would make the comment the subject.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build a close-friend chat reply: 'Yep, see you tomorrow.'
inlineExercises.explanation: ㅇㅇ is a casual yes/yeah used with close friends. It should not be used with teachers or formal contacts.

inlineExercises.prompt: Rewrite ㅇㅇ politely.
inlineExercises.explanation: 네, 알겠어요 is a safer polite reply. ㅇㅇ is too casual outside close chat.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix this professor reply: 'ㅇㅇ 레전드예요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: ㅇㅇ and 레전드 are too casual for a professor. 정말 인상적이었습니다 keeps the positive reaction but changes the register.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which abbreviation means “for real / seriously” in casual chat?
inlineExercises.explanation: ㄹㅇ is shorthand for real/seriously. ㅠㅠ shows crying, and ㅇㅈ means agreed.

bullets: ㅋㅋ laughs, ㅠㅠ cries or complains, ㅇㅇ says quick yes, ㄹㅇ marks for real, and ㅇㅈ agrees with a take.
완전, 진짜, 대박, 레전드, and 개웃겨 add casual intensity; they do not automatically become formal with 요.
Platform actions need Korean verbs: 댓글을 달다, 좋아요를 누르다, 친구한테 공유하다.
A close friend chat, live chat, professor message, and company post require different surfaces even when the feeling is the same.

writingTask.prompt: Reply to a friend's funny video in a casual KakaoTalk chat (2-3 lines): react with chat tokens and an intensifier, and mention a platform action.
writingTask.hint: Use chat tokens (ㅋㅋ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ) and intensifiers (완전/진짜/대박), plus a fixed platform phrase like 좋아요 누르다 or 공유하다.
writingTask.model:
ㅋㅋㅋ 이거 완전 레전드 ㄹㅇ 개웃겨
나도 방금 좋아요 눌렀어 ㅇㅇ
친구한테 공유했어
writingTask.modelEn: Hahaha this is totally legendary, for real so funny. I just hit like too, yeah. I shared it with a friend.

canDo: Read and use chat tokens like ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, ㅇㅈ in casual messages
Crank up the feeling with colloquial intensifiers (완전 / 진짜 / 대박 / 레전드)
Use fixed platform verb pairings (좋아요 누르다, 댓글 달다, 공유하다)
Switch register correctly — ㅇㅇ with friends vs 네 / 알겠어요 in formal replies

chapters.title: Synthesis and Production Review
chapters.goal: Put the whole course together in one message that fits the situation.
chapters.scenario: You switch between an interview answer, a formal email, coworker chat, and a KakaoTalk reply.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘 면접 답변, 이메일, 카톡 답장을 한 번에 검수해 볼까요?
dialogue.romanization: oneul myeonjeop dapbyeon, imeil, katok dapjangeul han beone geomsuhae bolkkayo?
dialogue.en: Shall we review today's interview answer, email, and KakaoTalk reply together?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 먼저 상황과 상대방을 정하고 문체를 맞춰야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: meonjeo sanghwanggwa sangdaebangeul jeonghago munchereul matchwoya haeyo.
dialogue.en: First, decide the situation and listener, then match the style.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 면접 답변은 높임말과 시제를 확인하고, 이메일은 연결어와 마무리를 봐요.
dialogue.romanization: myeonjeop dapbyeoneun nopimmalgwa sijereul hwaginhago, imeireun yeongyeoreowa mamurireul bwayo.
dialogue.en: For the interview answer, check honorifics and tense; for the email, check connectors and the closing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 카톡에서는 편하게 써도 되지만 회사 메일에는 ㅋㅋ를 빼야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: katogeseoneun pyeonhage sseodo doejiman hoesa meileneun kkreul ppaeya haeyo.
dialogue.en: You can write casually in KakaoTalk, but in a company email you need to remove ㅋㅋ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Lastly, I will check even each particle again.

chapters.guidedPractice: Choose one idea and produce it four ways: interview answer, formal email, coworker chat, and friend KakaoTalk. Check situation, listener, style, particles, tense, and connectors each time.
chapters.realLifeTask: Rewrite one idea for two different listeners, then check register, particles, tense, connectors, and closing.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a task and relationship. Say whether you need casual, polite, or formal Korean, then produce and revise one sentence.
chapters.review: Can you switch the same message between interview, email, coworker talk, and friend chat without leaving mismatched particles, tense, connectors, or slang?

beginnerGuide.title: Start with the situation
beginnerGuide.body: Do not start by translating English. First decide the purpose, listener, and channel: interview, email, coworker chat, or friend KakaoTalk.

beginnerGuide.title: Check five layers
beginnerGuide.body: After drafting, check 문체, 입자, 시제, 높임말, and 연결어. A sentence can have good vocabulary and still fail because one layer does not match the situation.

beginnerGuide.title: Rewrite, not decorate
beginnerGuide.body: Polite Korean is not casual Korean with 요 added. Rewrite rough slang, sentence endings, connectors, and closing phrases together.

checkpoints: I can choose the register before choosing vocabulary or endings.
I can check particles, tense, honorifics, connector, and closing in one pass.
I can rewrite the same meaning for formal email and casual chat.

curriculumTrack.label: C1 Written & Synthesis
curriculumTrack.description: Formal writing, internet register awareness, and whole-course production checks.

learningLayers.label: Core
learningLayers.purpose: Start here: these are the words and patterns you need for the main sentence.

learningLayers.label: Expand
learningLayers.purpose: Use these next so the same grammar works in more real situations.

learningLayers.label: Reference
learningLayers.purpose: Open these when a sentence feels confusing or you want to check the rule.

exitTask.canDo: Put the whole course together in one message that fits the situation.
exitTask.prompt: Rewrite one idea for two different listeners, then check register, particles, tense, connectors, and closing.

sampleAnswer.ko: 메일에서는 '확인해 주셔서 감사합니다'라고 쓰고, 친구에게는 '확인해 줘서 고마워'라고 할게요.
sampleAnswer.en: In an email I will write 'thank you for checking,' and to a friend I will say 'thanks for checking.'

checklist: I can choose the register before choosing vocabulary or endings.
I can check particles, tense, honorifics, connector, and closing in one pass.
I can rewrite the same meaning for formal email and casual chat.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

hook.situation: One day, four Korean tasks: answer an interview question, send a formal email, talk with coworkers, and reply to a friend on KakaoTalk. The grammar changes because the relationship changes.
objectives: Run a production checklist before sending or saying Korean.
Revise the same idea across interview, email, coworker talk, and friend chat.
Catch mismatches in particles, tense, honorifics, connectors, and style.
hook.whyItMatters: The final skill is not knowing more patterns. It is choosing the right Korean surface for the situation and then checking every layer before the sentence leaves your mouth or screen.

grammarNotes.title: Integrated production checklist
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Before producing Korean, ask: who is listening, what is the purpose, and what style does this channel require? Then check the grammar pieces.
grammarNotes.formation: Purpose -> listener -> channel -> style -> particles -> tense/aspect -> connectors -> closing.

examples.ko: 면접 답변은 정중하게 말하고, 경험의 시제를 흔들리지 않게 맞춰야 해요.
examples.romanization: myeonjeop dapbyeoneun jeongjunghage malhago, gyeongheomui sijereul heundeulliji anke matchwoya haeyo.
examples.en: For an interview answer, speak courteously and keep the tense of your experience consistent.
examples.note: Interview Korean checks register and tense together.

examples.ko: 공식 이메일에서는 확인 부탁드립니다처럼 마무리를 격식 있게 써야 해요.
examples.romanization: gongsik imeireseoneun hwagin butakdeurimnidacheoreom mamurireul gyeoksik itge sseoya haeyo.
examples.en: In a formal email, the closing should be formal, like 확인 부탁드립니다.
examples.note: Email Korean needs closing phrases, not only correct grammar.

examples.ko: 친구 카톡에서는 편하게 써도 되지만 회사 메일에는 ㅋㅋ를 빼야 해요.
examples.romanization: chingu katogeseoneun pyeonhage sseodo doejiman hoesa meileneun kkreul ppaeya haeyo.
examples.en: You can write casually in a friend's KakaoTalk chat, but you must remove ㅋㅋ from a company email.
examples.note: Same feeling, different style.

exceptions: Do not treat the checklist as a fixed word order. It is a review habit.
If one layer changes, recheck the others. Formalizing a sentence can change endings, vocabulary, connectors, and closing.

grammarNotes.title: Rewrite by relationship, not by adding 요
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Politeness is a system. Adding 요 to slang or casual sentence shape does not make the whole sentence appropriate.
grammarNotes.formation: Casual idea -> polite neutral sentence -> formal written sentence.

examples.ko: 친구: ㅇㅇ 확인했어. / 회사 메일: 네, 확인했습니다.
examples.romanization: chingu: ngng hwaginhaesseo. / hoesa meil: ne, hwaginhaetseumnida.
examples.en: Friend: Yep, I checked. / Company email: Yes, I have confirmed it.
examples.note: ㅇㅇ changes to 네, and the ending changes to -했습니다.

examples.ko: 친구: 그 영상 개웃겨. / 면접: 그 사례가 매우 인상적이었습니다.
examples.romanization: chingu: geu yeongsang gaeutgyeo. / myeonjeop: geu saryega maeu insangjeogieotseumnida.
examples.en: Friend: That video is hilarious. / Interview: That example was very impressive.
examples.note: The rough slang is rewritten, not decorated.

examples.ko: 친구: 늦어서 미안. / 공식 이메일: 답장이 늦어져 죄송합니다.
examples.romanization: chingu: neujeoseo mian. / gongsik imeil: dapjangi neujeojyeo joesonghamnida.
examples.en: Friend: Sorry I'm late. / Formal email: I apologize for the delayed reply.
examples.note: Formal email uses a different phrase and a different sentence shape.

exceptions: 요 can make a sentence polite, but it cannot make rough slang formal.
Some friendly workplace chats allow softer language, but official emails still need complete phrases.

grammarNotes.title: The three quiet failure points
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Learners often notice vocabulary errors, but native readers feel particle, tense, and connector errors first because those pieces control the sentence relationship.
grammarNotes.formation: After the sentence sounds meaningful, check: noun role, event time, and sentence relationship.

examples.ko: 이 문장은 뜻은 맞지만 입자가 어색해요.
examples.romanization: i munjangeun tteuseun matjiman ipjaga eosaekaeyo.
examples.en: The meaning of this sentence is right, but the particle is awkward.
examples.note: A common review comment.

examples.ko: 경험을 말할 때는 과거 시제를 안정적으로 유지해야 해요.
examples.romanization: gyeongheomeul malhal ttaeneun gwageo sijereul anjeongjeogeuro yujihaeya haeyo.
examples.en: When talking about experience, you need to keep the past tense stable.
examples.note: Interview answers often talk about past experience.

examples.ko: 공식 글에서는 그래서보다 따라서가 더 자연스러울 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: gongsik geureseoneun geuraeseoboda ttaraseoga deo jayeonseureoul su isseoyo.
examples.en: In formal writing, 따라서 can be more natural than 그래서.
examples.note: Connector choice depends on register and logic.

exceptions: A short friend chat can omit pieces that a formal email cannot omit.
A connector is not decoration. It must match result, contrast, clarification, or summary.

grammarNotes.title: One idea, four Korean versions
grammarNotes.mentalModel: A strong learner can keep the same message while changing the surface for each situation.
grammarNotes.formation: Message idea: I checked it and will revise it. Change the style by channel.

examples.ko: 면접: 관련 경험을 검토했고, 필요한 부분을 개선하겠습니다.
examples.romanization: myeonjeop: gwallyeon gyeongheomeul geomtohaetgo, piryohan bubuneul gaeseonhagetseumnida.
examples.en: Interview: I have reviewed the related experience and will improve the necessary parts.
examples.note: Formal speech with -겠습니다.

examples.ko: 이메일: 자료 확인 후 수정해서 다시 보내드리겠습니다.
examples.romanization: imeil: jaryo hwagin hu sujeonghaeseo dasi bonaedeurigetseumnida.
examples.en: Email: After checking the materials, I will revise them and send them again.
examples.note: Formal email with 보내드리겠습니다.

examples.ko: 동료 대화: 자료 확인했고, 필요한 부분은 다시 고칠게요.
examples.romanization: dongnyo daehwa: jaryo hwaginhaetgo, piryohan bubuneun dasi gochilgeyo.
